r0-convnext-coop-fp32-anchor.card:
id: r0-convnext-coop-fp32-anchor
parents: []
operation: new_design
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: ldg128
  st: direct
  grid: persistent
  launch: fused
  tile: rows128
  red: cta
  cache: default
  spec: all
hypothesis: >-
  Research anchor: one cooperative fp32 SIMT launch (296 persistent CTAs, two grid.sync()s) with three phases: channel-chunked
  depthwise 7x7 patch tiles writing K-major activations plus LayerNorm partial sums; 128x128/128x96/64x64/32x32 SIMT GEMM1
  with exact-erf GELU and per-image GRN sums; GEMM2 with the GRN affine applied to A, cross-CTA split-K atomics at small
  sizes and the residual added into NCHW. Correct on all 16 workloads; it exists to obtain Tb and Tsol.
expected_effect:
  S: {pct: -45, confidence: medium}
  M: {pct: -20, confidence: medium}
  L: {pct: -10, confidence: low}
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 128
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 70208
  threads_per_cta: 256
  ctas_per_sm: 2
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 65536
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs: {BM: 128, BN: 128, BK: 32, GEMM_CFGS: 4, SPLITK_MAX: 16, P1_PATCH: 4x4, NT: 256, GRID: 296}
tests: [H4, H5, H6]
findings:
  - "precision: with the harness generators (weights /sqrt(fan_in), LN weight ones) fp16/fp16 and tf32/tf32 GEMMs give err rms 4.5e-4 vs tol 2.4e-3..3.8e-3, 0.000% beyond tol over 6 workloads x 2 seeds; bf16 fails 28-50% [probe_b200]"
  - "fp32 SIMT peak: FFMA 67.7 TF/s and packed fma.f32x2 74.0 TF/s at 1965 MHz = 128 FMA/clk/SM either way; 56.8 TF/s at the 1500 MHz lock [probe_b200]"
  - "launch floor: empty kernel 1.8 us, +2.0 us per extra launch; 296-CTA atomic grid barrier ~1.5 us, 1184 CTAs ~5 us per barrier [probe_b200]"
  - "reference profile: 17-18 kernels per call; cuDNN depthwise conv 492 us, two simt sgemm 400+346 us, six GRN elementwise kernels ~190 us each at 32,128,64,64 [probe_b200]"
  - "cuBLAS fp32 sgemm both GEMMs (warm): 36-52 us at S sizes (8-28 TF/s), 2758 us at the largest (41-45 TF/s) [probe_b200]"
  - "v1 (all-channel dwconv tiles, [M][C] layout, transposed smem stores): 16/16 pass but 546 us at 1,192,28,28 and 2091 us at 2,768,7,7 because phase 1 ran on 1-28 CTAs [run_tests]"
  - "v2 (this kernel): 16/16 pass, 65-140 us at S, 124-353 us at M, 265-5596 us at L; still slower than the reference at 8,384,14,14, 16,384,14,14, 8,768..32,768,7,7 and 8,320,32,32 [run_tests]"
  - "v2 phase breakdown (separate launches): 32,768,7,7 P1 333 / P2 425 / P3 359 us; 64,96,112,112 544 / 2973 / 2709 us; GEMM phases 17-25 TF/s [probe_b200]"
  - "bare 128x128x32 SIMT core on the same shapes: 46-50 TF/s (unroll 1 best), 57-60 TF/s without global loads; lane layouts within 5% [probe_b200]"
  - "ablations: removing the GELU/store/warp-sum epilogue lifts P2 to 32-35 TF/s; removing the per-element GRN affine lifts P3 to 33-35 TF/s; prologue ~5%; launch_bounds(256,1) (238-255 regs) is slower everywhere [probe_b200]"
  - "phase 1: block-level weight transposes 42 us at C=768 vs 11.5 us warp-level; per-token conv 4 tokens/lane 306 us vs 1 token/lane 59 us at 32,768,7,7; zero-padded smem planes 35.5/12.7/32.4 us at 32,768,7,7 / 2,768,7,7 / 16,384,14,14 (correct to 1e-5); prefetching 4x4 patch conv 516 vs 549 us at the largest (FMA bound 134 us at 1500 MHz) [probe_b200]"
  - "dead end: cooperative single kernel measured 6717 us vs 6263 us for the same three phases as separate launches at the largest size (one comparison) [run_tests, probe_b200]"
paths:
  - {max_tokens: null, lang: cuda, width: 128, threads: 256, rows: 128, grid: persistent, mem: ldg, launches: 1, x: none, w: none, st: none, cluster: 1}
runs_on:
  H200: {runs: true, representative: true, note: "cooperative launch and cg grid sync work on sm_90; fp32 SIMT rate differs"}
  A100: {runs: true, representative: false, note: "needs cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel and 70 KB dynamic smem (ok on sm_80); ranking signal only"}
  L40S: {runs: true, representative: false, note: "100 KB smem per SM allows only 1 CTA/SM; correctness smoke test"}
risks:
  - "fp32 SIMT GEMMs are 10-30x off the FP16 tensor-core design that the tolerance permits; L-band times are 2-12x the stream floor"
  - "cooperative launch fails if the device cannot co-schedule sms x 2 CTAs at 70 KB smem each; grid is sized from the occupancy API at first call"
  - "split-K phase 3 relies on fp32 atomics into an x+b2-initialised output (non-deterministic summation order, within tolerance)"
  - "workspace up to 1.6 GB (hidden fp32 [4C][Mp]) allocated with torch.empty each call via the caching allocator"
measure_first: [H200]
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

r1-convnext-cluster16-dsmem.card:
id: r1-convnext-cluster16-dsmem
parents: [r0-convnext-coop-fp32-anchor]
operation: new_design
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: ldg128
  st: direct
  grid: oneshot
  launch: fused
  tile: token
  red: cta
  cache: default
  spec: dispatch:size
hypothesis: >-
  H13 (lineage C, E3): give each image (two 7x7 images when B >= 8) a 16-CTA cluster, so the GRN dependency stays
  inside one cluster. Each CTA owns C/16 channels (dwconv, LN, output) and hidden slice j (4C/16), held fp16 in smem.
  LN statistics, the fp16 LN tile, the GRN mean and the GEMM2 split-K partials move through DSMEM, with no grid barrier
  and no global intermediates; both GEMMs use swap-AB mma.sync f16. Measured result: correct (16/16) and 36-73% faster
  than the anchor on the six 7x7/14x14 rows, but REFUTED against the 30/45/40 us targets. The bounds are DSMEM at
  12-18 B/clk/SM (the reduce-scatter moves C*T*4 B per CTA whatever the cluster size), weight slices streamed from L2
  through registers at ~37 GB/s/SM, and only 7 concurrent 16-CTA clusters (B=32 at 7x7 needs 3 waves).
expected_effect:
  S: {pct: 0, confidence: high}
  M: {pct: -30, confidence: medium}
  L: {pct: -55, confidence: medium}
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 128
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 227000
  threads_per_cta: 512
  ctas_per_sm: 1
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 65536
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs: {CL_G: 16, CL_NT: 512, IPC: "2 if B>=8 and HW=49 else 1", R_rounds: 2, PF: 4, PF2_C384: 3, NB_cfgs: "(4,7) C768/IPC1, (7,13) C768/IPC2, (9,13) C384/14x14", CL_LB: 16}
dispatch:
  - {shapes: "C%128==0, (HW=49) or (HW=196, C=384)", kernel: cl_kernel, meta: {cluster: 16, threads: 512, smem: "115-227 KB"}}
  - {shapes: "all others", kernel: convnext_fused, meta: {cooperative: true, threads: 256, grid: 296}}
tests: [H13, H14, H12]
findings:
  - "probe (a): cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters at 256 thr: 16-CTA clusters 7 at 200 KB smem, 14 at 100 KB; 8-CTA clusters 15 at 200 KB, 33 at 100 KB (non-portable size allowed). Passes the >=6 rule for 16-CTA clusters, but B=32 at 7x7 still needs 3 waves of 16-CTA clusters [probe_b200]"
  - "probe (a): empty-kernel harness_time with 200 KB smem: plain 148x256 1.66 us; cluster launches 1.23 (16x4), 1.30 (16x8), 1.34 (16x16), 1.38 (8x16), 1.41 (8x32) us; cluster launch is not more expensive [probe_b200]"
  - "probe (b): DSMEM push all-gather of 74 KB (st.shared::cluster.v4, each CTA writes its slice to all): 5.5k clk with 16-CTA clusters (13.5 B/clk/SM), 4.05k clk with 8 (18.5 B/clk/SM); pull gather (ld.shared::cluster) 10.7k clk. At 1.5 GHz: 3.7 us (16 CTAs, fails the 3 us kill) and 2.7 us (8 CTAs) [probe_b200]"
  - "probe (b): DSMEM reduce-scatter reading 128-137 KB of fp32 partials with 16-deep load ILP: 11.6-12.2k clk (16 CTAs), 8.9k (8 CTAs), about 12 B/clk/SM; barrier.cluster arrive+wait about 375 clk. The volume is C*T*4 B per CTA independent of cluster size, so this term cannot shrink by changing the cluster size [probe_b200]"
  - "probe (c) H14 SUPPORTED: TMA through a TFLOAT32 tensor map rounds to nearest even, bit-exact: low13 0x1000 tie with even kept bit goes down, 0x3000 tie with odd goes up, 0x1001/0x17ff/0x1800/0x1fff go up, 0x0fff goes down. A FLOAT32 map leaves the bits unchanged [probe_b200]"
  - "probe H12: mma.sync.m16n8k16 f16 with f32 accumulate reaches 2018-2046 FLOP/clk/SM with 4-16 warps and 8 independent chains, i.e. 454 TF/s at 1.5 GHz (1/4 of kind::f16 tcgen05) [probe_b200]"
  - "probe: red.global.add.f32 into L2 reaches 4.1-4.4 TB/s of fp32 adds with 256-512 CTAs and 1.0 TB/s with 32 CTAs (launch included); the v4 form is no faster than scalar [probe_b200]"
  - "dead end / pitfall: a runtime guard `if (jj < nb)` around mma.sync makes nvcc wrap every HMMA in WARPSYNC.ALL + BRA, costing ~470 clk per k-block. GEMM1 with loads removed took 23.5 us; with NB as a template parameter, 6.4 us (NB=4) and 10.7 us (NB=7). A 13-way switch over NB made the full kernel slower still (2,768,7,7: 123 -> 147 us); per-shape templates with padded token tiles fixed it [probe_b200, run_tests]"
  - "pitfall: the zero-padded plane fill (one __ldg then one smem store per loop iteration) serialised on DRAM latency, taking 15-20 us for 48 planes; issuing 16 loads before the stores removes it [probe_b200]"
  - "kill criterion hit: streaming a 590 KB W1 slice through registers (PF=4, 16 warps, 128 regs) runs at ~37 GB/s/SM. GEMM1 per CTA at C=768 takes 15-20 us rented (14 us with NB=13 on 12 warps), above the 12 us limit; deeper register prefetch (PF=8) spills and is slower (51-66 us). The smem that a cp.async/TMA weight ring would need is taken by the a tile and the hidden slice [probe_b200]"
  - "v1 phase profile at 2,768,7,7, cold (globaltimer, CTA medians): conv 20 us, LN gather 6 + barrier 1.7, GEMM1 52, GRN 7, GEMM2 round 0 17, reduce + round 1 25, total 129 us; the anchor takes 124 us [probe_b200]"
  - "final run_tests (rented, unlocked clocks), 16/16 PASS: 2,768,7,7 79.4 (anchor 123.8); 8,768,7,7 117.3 (263.7); 16,768,7,7 224.1 (582.0); 32,768,7,7 333.2 (1214.8); 8,384,14,14 173.8 (271.7); 16,384,14,14 259.5 (352.6); other 10 rows unchanged within 2%. Emulator-predicted portal score 0.351 +- 0.008, vs 0.304 for the anchor [run_tests]"
  - "verdict H13: refuted for the <=30-45 us goal. At 7 concurrent clusters, ~12 B/clk/SM of DSMEM and 454 TF/s of mma.sync, the floor is about 50-60 us per cluster wave at C=768. A recovery would need tcgen05 plus a TMA weight ring, and the a tile and hidden slice already fill the 227 KB of smem [INFERRED from the probes]"
paths:
  - {max_tokens: 1568, lang: cuda, width: 128, threads: 512, rows: 49, grid: oneshot, mem: ldg, launches: 1, x: none, w: none, st: none, cluster: 16}
  - {max_tokens: null, lang: cuda, width: 128, threads: 256, rows: 128, grid: persistent, mem: ldg, launches: 1, x: none, w: none, st: none, cluster: 1}
runs_on:

  A100: {runs: false, representative: false, note: "no clusters/DSMEM on sm_80"}
  L40S: {runs: false, representative: false, note: "no clusters on sm_89; 100 KB smem"}
risks:
  - "Uses 16-CTA thread-block clusters (non-portable) as a GEMM split; the ledger constraint limits clusters to GEMM tiles that need them, and #38 saw 2-5% portal losses with large clustered grids. Needs operator review before a portal slot."
  - "The GRN affine is applied to the fp16 hidden in place (two fp16 roundings on GEMM2's B operand); passes 16/16, but margin is somewhat below the simulated single-rounding 5 sigma."
  - "227 KB smem at C=768 with IPC=2 and at C=384 14x14 (1 CTA/SM); any change to padding or the small region can overflow."
  - "B=32 at 7x7 runs 16 clusters in 3 waves (7 concurrent), so time grows linearly with B."
measure_first: [H200]
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

task.instructions: Experiment E3 (tests H13): Cluster-per-image kernel for the 7x7 and 14x14 rows (hidden slices in smem, DSMEM reductions, no grid barrier), with cluster-occupancy, DSMEM and TFLOAT32-rounding probes; other shapes dispatched to the anchor path. Step 0 probes (<= 20 min, record each as a finding): (a) cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters for cluster sizes 8 and 16 (cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed) with 200 KB dynamic smem and 256 threads per CTA: how many clusters run concurrently and the launch-to-first-instruction latency under harness timing; (b) DSMEM microbench in clocks: 16 CTAs all-gather a 75 KB fp16 tile (each writes its 1/16 into every CTA via st.shared::cluster) and reduce-scatter 16 x [768 x 49] fp32 partials (each CTA reads 15 slices via ld.shared::cluster); (c) H14: TMA-load fp32 values with chosen low mantissa bits through a TFLOAT32 tensor map and check bit-exactly whether the result is round-to-nearest or truncation. If (a) gives fewer than 6 concurrent 16-CTA clusters, use 8-CTA clusters (two clusters per image pair is not allowed; use 8 slices of 4C/8). Step 1 kernel, for 2/8/16/32,768,7,7 and 8/16,384,14,14 (dispatch every other shape to the anchor's cooperative kernel copied from the r0 baseline): one cluster per image (two 7x7 images per cluster when B >= 8), CTA j owns C/G channels for the dwconv (zero-padded smem planes) and hidden slice j of 4C/G. LN: per-token partial sums exchanged through DSMEM (one cluster barrier), each CTA normalises its channels and writes the fp16 a tile [tokens][C] into every CTA's smem via st.shared::cluster (second barrier). GEMM1 swap-AB: A = W1 slice [4C/G x C] (fp32 from global/L2 converted to fp16 in smem, or TF32 if (c) confirms rounding), B = a^T, N = tokens; use whichever engine you can get correct in the session (mma.sync FP16 is acceptable; tcgen05 is not required for the thesis). GELU (exact erf) in registers; gf_k = sqrt(sum over tokens of h^2) is thread-local per hidden channel; one DSMEM reduce of the per-CTA partial sums of gf gives mean_k gf (third barrier); s_k = 1 + gw_k*gf_k/(mean+eps), h' = s_k*h + gb_k in registers, written fp16 to the CTA's own smem. GEMM2 partial: W2[:, slice] [C x 4C/G] x h'^T -> [C x tokens] fp32; reduce across the cluster by DSMEM reduce-scatter (CTA j finalises output channels j*C/G .. (j+1)*C/G: + b2 + x, store NCHW with lanes along hw). Weights: each CTA reads only its two slices (1.2 MB at C=768) and ideally once per cluster via TMA multicast or plain L2 reads; measure which. Time each phase in clocks for one cluster at 32,768,7,7 and compare with the 12 us kill criterion from the probe. run_tests on all 16 workloads x 10 rounds; report per-workload rented times. Success: 16/16 pass; rented <= 30 us at 2,768,7,7 and 8,768,7,7, <= 45 us at 16,768,7,7 and 32,768,7,7, <= 40 us at 8/16,384,14,14 (anchor: 124-1217 us); projected portal score >= 0.50 with the other 10 rows still on the anchor path; probe numbers (concurrent clusters, DSMEM gather/reduce clocks, TFLOAT32 rounding) recorded. Refuted if: fewer than 4 concurrent 8-CTA clusters, or weight-slice ingest plus one GEMM1 per CTA > 12 us at 32,768,7,7 under harness timing, or DSMEM all-gather of the 75 KB a tile > 3 us; any of these means the cluster path cannot beat ~30 us per row and the lineage is retired after incubation with the probe numbers as its conclusions. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

r1-convnext-coop-hmma-ring.card:
id: r1-convnext-coop-hmma-ring
parents: [r0-convnext-coop-fp32-anchor]
operation: structural_mutation
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: cpasync
  st: direct
  grid: persistent
  launch: fused
  tile: rows128
  red: cta
  cache: default
  spec: all
hypothesis: >-
  Lineage B, E2 (H12). Legacy mma.sync.m16n8k16 FP16 with fp32 accumulate runs at 2048 FLOP/clk/SM, which is
  0.455 PF/s at 1.5 GHz, so the GEMMs stop being the bottleneck except at the top two sizes. The kernel stays one
  cooperative launch: phase 1 does the weight pass (fp16, native [N][K] layout; LN and gb folded into row sums) and
  the dwconv, writing raw fp16 d and LN partials; GEMM1 uses a 4-stage cp.async ring with the LN algebra in the
  epilogue, then GELU and fp16 hidden plus GRN sums; GEMM2 uses a 4-stage ring with the GRN scale as an smem pass,
  then the residual. Rented B200: 16/16 pass, -59/-65/-74 % vs the anchor in S/M/L; projected portal score 0.561.
expected_effect:
  S: {pct: -59, confidence: medium}
  M: {pct: -65, confidence: medium}
  L: {pct: -74, confidence: medium}
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 128
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 106272
  threads_per_cta: 256
  ctas_per_sm: 2
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 151552
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs:
  NT: 256
  GRID: 296
  GEMM_CFGS: "128x128/128x96/64x64(KS2)/32x32(KS8,BK16)"
  STAGES: 4
  BK: 32
  TABK: 1024
  P1_CPW: "4, or 1 for patch tiles when 32-ch tiles < grid"
tests: [H12, H11, H4, H5, H17]
findings:
  - "H12 supported: mma.sync m16n8k16 f16->f32 = 2048 FLOP/clk/SM with 1 CTA/SM (4-16 warps, 8 or 16 independent chains) = 0.455 PF/s at 1.5 GHz, 1/4 of tcgen05 kind::f16; wall 520-546 TF/s at boost. Per-CTA clock64 with 2 CTAs/SM gives bogus 2700-4090 (CTAs not co-resident) [probe_b200]"
  - "H11 fixed floor F: this kernel with all three phases stubbed (296 CTAs, 104 KB smem, 2 grid.sync) = 4.2-4.7 us on every shape; three plain launches stubbed = 9.7-10.1 us [probe_b200 harness_time]"
  - "H4: full kernel, coop vs three plain launches, 3 interleaved repeats: 1,192,28,28 29.7 vs 36.3 us; 2,768,7,7 46.7 vs 50.2; 64,96,112,112 1793 vs 1749 (coop 2.5% slower at the largest). Regs: 128 for all four kernel variants (PH0 has 64 B spill) [probe_b200]"
  - "H5: split-K auto vs forced 1: 1,192,28,28 29.9 vs 30.6 us (no effect); 2,768,7,7 46.5 vs 64.6; 8,768,7,7 86.1 vs 120.6 (split worth 28-29% at C=768) [probe_b200]"
  - "run_tests (rented B200, us): 1,192 30.9; 1,96 28.3; 1,160,449,7 55.2; 2,96 42.2; 4,192 47.2; 8,384 85.8; 4,96 62.5; 8,192 66.1; 16,384 113.0; 2,768 47.9; 8,768 87.1; 16,768 107.9; 8,320 175.3; 32,768 179.5; 32,128 587.2; 64,96 1786.6; projected portal 0.561 +- 0.008 [run_tests]"
  - "per-phase (cumulative masks, includes F ~4.6): 1,192,28,28 P1 13.2 / +P2 20.1 / all 29.7; 1,160,449,7 17.1/30.6/56.4; 2,768,7,7 19.7/33.2/47.1; 32,768,7,7 48.2/106.0/180.6; 32,128,64,64 107/309/586; 64,96,112,112 446/1290/1793 [probe_b200]"
  - "precision: err rms 3.9-4.2e-4, max 1.9-2.8e-3, <=1e-7 fraction beyond atol 2.4e-3 with randomized lnw/lnb (stricter than harness); raw fp16 d with LN folded into the GEMM1 epilogue (r*(acc - mu*s1) + c1) is as accurate as an fp16 LN'd operand [probe_b200]"
  - "phase-1 parallelism: 8-channel tiles (1 channel per warp) when 32-channel tiles < grid cut P1 at 1,192,28,28 from ~25 us to ~9 us; the 4x4 register-patch conv is latency-bound (10 serial row loads per channel), so tile count matters more than FMA rate at S [probe_b200]"
  - "dead end: applying 8-ch tiles to the 7x7 smem-plane path made the GEMM1 prologue sum 96 partials per token serially (P1+P2 at 8,768,7,7 61 -> 93 us); planes keep 32-ch tiles and the prologue now splits partials over NT/BM threads per token [probe_b200]"
  - "dead end: cp.async-staged smem bands for the dwconv (per-warp double buffer, 16B interior + 4B halo cp.async, float4 LDS) were slower than direct __ldg 4x4 patches: P1 41 vs 29 us at 1,192,28,28 and 515 vs 385 us at 64,96,112,112 (cause not isolated) [probe_b200]"
  - "GEMM main loop: register-prefetched 1-deep A -> 4-stage pure cp.async rings (LN algebra in epilogue, GRN as in-smem scale pass) cut P2 at 8,384,14,14 from ~31 to ~21 us but barely moved the largest (950 -> 888 us), where each tile is a serial prologue/3-chunk/GELU-epilogue chain [probe_b200]"
  - "GEMM2 epilogue: issuing all residual x loads of a tile before use (NPT registers) cut P3 at 64,96,112,112 from 896 to 504 us [probe_b200]"
  - "weight pass at C=768 (fp16 conversion + row sums, 19 MB) costs ~10 us of P1 (P1 with only the weight pass = 14.8-15.5 us vs F 4.6) [probe_b200]"
  - "success criteria: S rows <= 45 us missed at 1,160,449,7 (55) and 4,192,28,28 (47); 2,768,7,7 47.9 <= 60 met; 32,768,7,7 179.5 > 150 missed; largest 1787 <= 2500 met; F 4.6 <= 15 and HMMA 0.455 >= 0.15 PF/s, so neither refutation clause fires [run_tests, probe_b200]"

task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H12): Anchor with mma.sync FP16 GEMM cores, fp16 transposed weights and the measured phase-1 fixes; probes for the HMMA rate, the fixed floor, coop vs three launches and split-K. Launch sequence per call, identical for a given shape: K1 custom: depthwise 7x7 conv + bias + LayerNorm -> A1 fp16 [M][C] row-major (use zero-padded smem planes per warp for W<=14, register patches or TMA-free float4 rows otherwise; LN needs all C per token so tile tokens x all channels); extra blocks of K1 convert W1 -> fp16 [4C][C] and W2 -> fp16 [C][4C] with cvt.rn.f16x2 and compute b2' = b2 + W2*gb (GEMV). GEMM1: cublasLtMatmul fp16 x fp16, fp32 compute, BIAS epilogue (b1), output fp16 or fp32 [M][4C] (fp16 only if run_tests passes 16/16; report max err both ways). K2 custom: exact erf GELU (erff, not tanh), write h fp16 [M][4C], per-(image,k) sum of squares via warp reduce + atomics into a [B][4C] fp32 workspace zeroed by K1. K3 custom: s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*sqrt(gf2)/(mean_k sqrt(gf2) + eps) and apply it: when B*C*4C*2 bytes <= 16 MB write W2_b = W2*diag(s_b) fp16 per image, else scale h rows in place (half2). GEMM2: strided-batched cublasLtMatmul computing D_b^T [C][HW] = W2_b [C][4C] x h_b^T so D lands directly in NCHW, beta=1 with C operand = x_b (stride C*HW) and D = output_b, bias b2' per output channel (either in the epilogue or pre-added to the C operand by K1 writing output = x + b2' and using beta=1 with C == D). task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H15): Library pipeline: custom dwconv+LN, cuBLASLt FP16 GEMMs with fused bias/residual, fp16 hidden, strided-batched NCHW output. Build a C++ solution (languages cuda_cpp + cublas; add -lcublasLt -lcublas to ld_flags; binding.cpp + kernel.cu layout; the cuBLASLt handle, matmul descriptors and the per-shape algorithm table are module-level caches keyed on (B,C,H,W) only, created on first call with cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic and never re-tuned). Launch sequence per call, identical for a given shape: K1 custom: depthwise 7x7 conv + bias + LayerNorm -> A1 fp16 [M][C] row-major (use zero-padded smem planes per warp for W<=14, register patches or TMA-free float4 rows otherwise; LN needs all C per token so tile tokens x all channels); extra blocks of K1 convert W1 -> fp16 [4C][C] and W2 -> fp16 [C][4C] with cvt.rn.f16x2 and compute b2' = b2 + W2*gb (GEMV). GEMM1: cublasLtMatmul fp16 x fp16, fp32 compute, BIAS epilogue (b1), output fp16 or fp32 [M][4C] (fp16 only if run_tests passes 16/16; report max err both ways). K2 custom: exact erf GELU (erff, not tanh), write h fp16 [M][4C], per-(image,k) sum of squares via warp reduce + atomics into a [B][4C] fp32 workspace zeroed by K1. K3 custom: s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*sqrt(gf2)/(mean_k sqrt(gf2) + eps) and apply it: when B*C*4C*2 bytes <= 16 MB write W2_b = W2*diag(s_b) fp16 per image, else scale h rows in place (half2). GEMM2: strided-batched cublasLtMatmul computing D_b^T [C][HW] = W2_b [C][4C] x h_b^T so D lands directly in NCHW, beta=1 with C operand = x_b (stride C*HW) and D = output_b, bias b2' per output channel (either in the epilogue or pre-added to the C operand by K1 writing output = x + b2' and using beta=1 with C == D). All workspaces from torch.empty in run(). Then measure, under harness timing on the rented B200: (1) per-launch times at 1,192,28,28; 2,768,7,7; 32,768,7,7; 32,128,64,64; 64,96,112,112; (2) for GEMM1/GEMM2 at every one of the 16 shapes, the top-3 heuristic algorithms, FP16 operands vs CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32 on the fp32 A1/W (no conversion kernel): pick the faster per shape into the table and record both; (3) the H16 probe: a kernel that writes then reads back a 20, 42 and 134 MB fp16 scratch after the harness's 2xL2 zero-fill, versus the same kernel with no scratch, to price the hidden round trip per size. run_tests on all 16 workloads x 10 rounds; report per-workload rented times, not band geomeans. Success: 16/16 pass; rented time <= 40 us on every S/M row (1,192 .. 2,768), <= 80 us at 8/16/32,768,7,7, <= 700 us at the largest; run_tests projected portal score >= 0.60; the per-launch breakdown and the H15/H16 numbers are recorded as findings. Refuted if: cuBLASLt GEMM1+GEMM2 together exceed 20 us at the S shapes for every heuristic algorithm (then the library floor caps the lineage near 0.6 and r2 replaces the GEMMs with custom tensor-core kernels), or the H16 probe shows the fp16 hidden round trip costs > 10 us at 8,320,32,32. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

task.instructions:
Experiment E1 (tests H41): Balanced image-straddling token-range tiles, no g, scale-in-smem GEMM2 for the six tc rows. Budget: 18 B200 minutes, 90 min wall. Parent = r9-d-e1-asynca (the default tc path in r9-merge); r9-d-e2-pair-smemg is in your lineage too (reuse its 'one producer warp owns a whole stage, stages round-robin over warps' signalling). Keep every sc row and the sc_kernel untouched; keep the old tc path in the file so that any tc row where the new path loses stays on the r9 code (per-row dispatch by shape).

STEP 0 (<= 2 B200 min, answers the premise audit): (a) read tc_kernel's flat self-resetting barrier: the arriving side must be __syncthreads then one thread red.release.gpu (or __threadfence + atomicAdd); the waiting side must spin with ld.acquire.gpu, then execute fence.proxy.async (so the CTA's later TMA reads of d/h/scratch written by other CTAs' generic stores are ordered), then __syncthreads. Add whatever is missing. (b) cuobjdump -res-usage on the shipped parent build: STACK must be 0 for tc_kernel and sc_kernel; record registers. (c) 1500-call stress loop at 8,768 and 16,384 against the fp32 torch reference (max |err| must stay <= the r8 log + 1e-4 on every call). If (a)-(c) show anything, revert tc_kernel to cg grid.sync and report; otherwise record 'barrier verified'.

STEP 1: flat token layouts. d scratch becomes [C][B*HW] fp16 and h becomes [4C][B*HW] fp16 with no per-image padding (the conv unit's stores and the TMA maps change; token = b*HW + hw). TMA box starts along the token axis must be multiples of 8 tokens (16 B).

STEP 2: tile tables per tc row (host, shape-only): GEMM1 tiles = hidden tiles x token ranges, ranges = ceil(ceil(B*HW / R) / 8) * 8 tokens with (hidden tiles x R) <= 148: 16,384 12 x 12 (264 tokens, N = 272 as two MMAs 128 + 144 into adjacent TMEM columns); 32,768 24 x 6 (264); 16,768 24 x 6 (136, N = 144); 8,768 24 x 6 (72, N = 80); 8,384 12 x 12 (136, N = 144); 2,768 only if time remains (24 x 5 ranges of 24 tokens, N = 32), otherwise it stays on the parent path (24.0 us). Epilogue per tile: LN fold + A&S GELU as now; the sumsq per (image, k) is accumulated in registers per image segment (image = token / HW, at most 2 segments at 14x14 and 6-7 at 7x7 per 264-token range; the 4-way image select exists) and red.add-ed into gsum[B][4C] (fp32, zeroed in phase A before sync 1); h stores only (no g, no gf in the epilogue). GEMM2 units = out-channel tiles x token ranges x KS with the same balancing (<= 148 units per pass, or 2 per CTA where unavoidable).

STEP 3: GEMM2 with one accumulator (N = range, two MMAs when > 256). After sync 2 each CTA computes, for the <= 7 images its units touch, gf[k] = sqrt(gsum[b][k]) and mean_k gf (one block reduction per image over 4C values), then s[b][k] = 1 + gw[k] * gf[k] / (mean + eps) for its K slices into smem (<= 7 x 768 fp32). Ring: A 16 KB + B (64 k x N x 2 B) per 64-k stage, as many stages as fit (>= 4). The stage-owner producer warp (round-robin over 4 producer warps, >= 2 stages ahead of the MMA warp) waits for the stage's TMA landing, multiplies the B tile in place by s[img(token)][k] (each k row is 128 contiguous bytes per 64-token chunk in the SW128 layout; 16-B vectors of 8 tokens can straddle an image boundary at HW = 49 or 196, so select per element), then fence.proxy.async.shared::cta and arrives on the ready barrier. Epilogue: out[b][c][hw] via the existing per-token addressing (red.add for KS > 1 into the x + b2' prefill).

STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 (portal-order re-runs); interleave x3 in one container vs r9-merge on the six tc rows; globaltimer stamps of GEMM1 end (median / max) at 16,384 and GEMM2 per-stage time at 8,768; cuobjdump STACK 0; PRECISION LOG over 10 seeded rounds (fp64 reference, harness generators) for every tc row the new path ships (the hidden is now rounded twice). If any row has a beyond-atol element, switch that row's B operand to the hi/lo fp16 split and re-log. Ship the new path only on rows where it wins; report per-row rented times and the stamps.

Optional if >= 3 B200 min remain: createpolicy evict_first on the W1/W2 fp32 loads in phase A, interleaved x3 at 8,768 / 32,768 (ship if >= 0.7 us). Success: In-container vs r9-merge: 16,384 <= 44 us and at least one of 32,768 <= 56, 8,384 <= 30.5, 16,768 <= 39.5, 8,768 <= 30; GEMM1 end (max over CTAs) at 16,384 >= 4 us earlier than the parent's; run_tests 16/16; precision log 0 beyond own atol on every shipped row. Refuted if: At 16,384 the GEMM1 end (max over CTAs) is less than 2 us earlier than the parent's despite one tile per CTA, or the in-place B scale makes GEMM2 stages > 1.3x the parent's stage time at 8,768 with >= 2 stages of look-ahead, or the new path wins no tc row by >= 1.5 us in-container. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid-barrier counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; cuBLASLt (if any) caches only the per-shape heuristic. No converted weights or other state kept between calls.

task.instructions:
Experiment E2 (tests H42): Custom tcgen05 GEMM2 launch replaces K3 + cuBLASLt G2 at 8,320 and 4,96 (4 launches -> 3). Budget: 18 B200 minutes, 90 min wall. Keep g_tc (pass 1), K0 and the 64,96 / 32,128 path (g_pass1 + K3 + cuBLASLt G2) unchanged; the new kernel is dispatched for 8,320 and 4,96 only.

STEP 0 (host/K0, no probe): K0 additionally writes fp16 W2 as [C][4C] row-major (K-major for the swap-AB A operand; TMA SW128 boxes of 128 rows x 64 k) and b2'[c] = sum_k W2[c][k] * gb[k] + b2[c] in fp32 (320 dot products of length 1280; one warp per c). Keep K0 at its current 3.5-4.5 us (check with harness_time).

STEP 1: g_g2 kernel, 1SM tcgen05 kind::f16, swap-AB, using your validated recipe (idesc, K-major SW128 A box SBO 1024 +32 B per k16, MN-major B 64-token chunks LBO = 64 k x 128 B, SBO 1024, +2048 per k16, tcgen05.ld 32x32b). Units = (c-tile, image, token chunk): 8,320 c-tiles 128 / 128 / 64 (the last via M=64 or a masked 128-row tile with TMA zero fill), 8 images x 4 chunks of 256 tokens = 96 units, N = 256 (one MMA per k16, 256 TMEM columns); 4,96 one c-tile of 96 rows (masked), chunks of 224 tokens (56 units) or 112 (112 units): time both. B = the pass-1 h_b array [K2 = 4C + 8][HW] per image (ignore the 8 augmentation rows: K = 4C exactly). Prologue per CTA: load gsum[b][0..4C) (the red.add sums pass 1 already writes), gf = sqrt, block-reduce mean_k, s[k] = 1 + gw[k] * gf[k] / (mean + eps) into smem (4C fp32), plus b2' for the c-tile. Ring: 4-6 stages of A 16 KB + B 32 KB (N = 256). Four producer warps, each owning a whole stage round-robin (>= 2 stages ahead of the MMA warp): wait for the TMA landing, scale the B tile in place by s[k] (each k row is 128 contiguous bytes per 64-token chunk; cvt to f32, multiply, cvt back, 16-B vectors), fence.proxy.async.shared::cta, arrive. One MMA warp with elect.sync, commit to the accumulator barrier. Stamp (globaltimer + clock64, from the MMA warp) the clk per 128x256x16 instruction at 8,320 and report it (audit item: does 1SM reach the ~256 clk ideal at N = 256 with TMA-fed operands?). Epilogue on all non-producer warps: tcgen05.ld, out[b][c][hw] = x[b][c][hw] + acc + b2'[c]; stage each 128-row x 256-token tile through the (now free) ring smem so that global reads of x and stores of out are 128-B-coalesced along hw (NCHW rows are contiguous for HW = 1024 / 3136).

STEP 2: validate g_g2 standalone against torch (fp32 reference of x + W2 (h * s) + b2') at both rows; then harness_time of the 3-launch pipeline vs the 4-launch parent interleaved x3 in one container at 8,320 and 4,96, plus g_g2 standalone cold (after the 2xL2 flush).

STEP 3: run_tests 16/16 (portal-order re-runs; the other 12 rows run the r0 anchor as a merge-only candidate), cuobjdump STACK 0 and <= 128 regs, PRECISION LOG over 10 seeded rounds (fp64 reference, harness generators) at 8,320 (atol 2.4e-3, the tightest row) and 4,96: the hidden is now rounded twice (fp16 h then fp16(h * s)). If any element is beyond atol + 1e-5|ref|, switch to the hi/lo B split (B_hi = fp16(h*s), B_lo = fp16(h*s - B_hi), two MMAs per k16) or scale the A tile per unit from fp32 W2 instead, re-log, and report the cost.

Stretch if >= 5 B200 min remain: dispatch g_g2 at 32,128 too (32 images x 16 chunks, persistent over 512 units) and compare with K3 + cuBLASLt (7.5 + 48.4 us); ship there only if faster in-container. Success: g_g2 standalone cold <= 9 us at 8,320 and <= 4.5 us at 4,96; rows in-container vs the parent 8,320 <= 49 us and 4,96 <= 31 us rented; run_tests 16/16; precision log 0 beyond own atol at both rows. Refuted if: g_g2 standalone cold > 14 us at 8,320 after the ring and epilogue are tuned (no better than K3 + cuBLASLt minus a launch), or the in-place B scale holds stages > 1.5x the N=256 MMA ideal with 2 stages of look-ahead, or the twice-rounded hidden fails the 10-round log at 8,320 and both fallbacks cost more than the K3 + G2 pair they replace. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid-barrier counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; cuBLASLt (if any) caches only the per-shape heuristic. No converted weights or other state kept between calls.

  - "v1 stamps at 8,320 (probe, g_g2 after a 2xL2 flush, us from first CTA start, medians): phase P end 7.4 (about 6 serial DRAM rounds for gsum, gw, W2 rows and gb), barrier out 9.7, first stage ready 11.5, epilogue start 20.0, end 23.6; g_g2 alone 26.3 us, full chain (K0+P1+g_g2) 64.8 vs K0+P1 38.4 [probe_b200]"

  - "v3 (shipped: b2' moved to K0, which also warms W2 into L2; both W2 rows per warp prefetched; 4,96 N=112): run_tests 16/16 incl. portal-order re-runs; 8,320 62.1 vs 58.5 us (+6.1 %), 4,96 37.4 vs 37.2 (tie), 64,96 / 32,128 unchanged code (864.4 / 227.2 vs 864.2 / 227.0) [run_tests]"

  - "What would be needed to win at 8,320: drop the grid barrier by building A_b per (c-tile, image) in a 4-CTA group (dataflow counters, or a cluster of the 4 token-chunk units sharing a TMA multicast of A), or pair the GEMM (cta_group::2, M = 256 = 2 c-tiles, half the B ingest per SM) so the mainloop reaches ~512 clk per stage; together worth ~8-10 us of the 23. [compile_b200, run_tests]"

task.instructions:
Experiment E3 (tests H43): New design: top-row pass 1 at the pipe bounds (bulk-staged register-blocked conv on FMA, tcgen05 GEMM1, GELU epilogue warps) for 64,96 and 32,128. Budget: 18 B200 minutes, 90 min wall. You start a new lineage (I) and may read only the r0 baseline, the lab notebook and the lineage conclusions; the notebook holds everything you need: the tcgen05 recipe (H r8: idesc = (1<<4)|(1<<16)|(N>>3)<<17|(128>>4)<<24, K-major SW128 A box SBO 1024 +32 B per k16, MN-major B [channel][token] 64-token chunks LBO = C*128, SBO 1024, +2048 per k16, tcgen05.ld 32x32b.x32), G r9's writer address functions for d written by plain st.shared into the SW128 B layout (A image byte = r*128 + (((c>>3) ^ (r&7))<<4) + (c&7)*2; B byte = (t>>6)*LBO + c*128 + ((((t&63)>>3) ^ (c&7))<<4) + (t&7)*2), the GRN tail (red.add per tile into a [B][4C] gsum zeroed by K0; a GRN-scale launch building per-image fp16 W2_b = fp16(W2 * s_b) and b2' hi/lo columns, grid (B, C/16), one row per warp, __launch_bounds__(512,2); cuBLASLt batched swap-AB GEMM2: A = h_b [K2 = 4C + 8][HW] fp16 per image with two constant 1,1 rows, B = W2_b [C][K2], C = x_b, D = out, beta 1, writes NCHW; ~6.6 TB/s at these rows), and the precision rules (d16, fp16(lnw*W1), h16 once, A&S erfc GELU; log 10 seeded rounds vs fp64). Target rows: 64,96,112,112 and 32,128,64,64 only; every other row runs the r0 anchor (merge-only candidate).

GATE (STEP 1, <= 5 B200 min): conv-only kernel at 64,96. Persistent CTAs of 16 warps, 1 CTA/SM, tile = R=2 image rows x W tokens x all C channels (224 tokens at 64,96; use R=3, 192 tokens at 32,128); each CTA takes a contiguous run of strips so halo rows hit L2. One TMA warp streams x in channel groups: for each group of 12 (64,96) or 16 (32,128) channels, (R+6) rows x W x 4 B per channel by 1-D cp.async.bulk (3.6 KB per channel at W=112) into a 2-stage ring (~43 KB per stage) with mbarrier expect_tx; zero rows at the image top/bottom are handled by predication, left/right zero padding by the tap loop. Eight conv warps compute register-blocked 2x8 output patches per lane (49 taps per channel in registers via __ldg from a K0-padded [C][7][8] buffer, inputs from LDS, ~7 FMA per LDS) and write fp16 d straight into the MN-major SW128 B tile (double-buffered, 43 KB each) plus per-token sum / sumsq partials in smem (fp32 of the fp16-rounded d). Measure with globaltimer and harness_time after the 2xL2 flush: conv-only pass over the whole 64,96 tensor (writing d tiles but no MMA / epilogue). Bound: 102 us at 1.95 GHz. Report rented us and the clock.

STEP 2 (only if STEP 1 <= 250 us; otherwise spend the remaining time on diagnosing the conv and report): add the GEMM: K0 writes W1' = fp16(lnw * W1) [4C][C] and u/v fold vectors; one MMA warp issues kind::f16 128 x N x 16 against A = W1' boxes 128 hidden x 64 k (K=96: 64 + 32) streamed per tile by TMA into a 2 x 16 KB ring (per-SM ingest ~74 KB per tile, negligible), 3 hidden blocks (4 at C=128) into two 224-column TMEM slots ping-ponged (slot reuse as G did). Six epilogue warps per finished block: tcgen05.ld, LN fold z = rs*(acc - mu*u) + v, A&S erfc GELU (do NOT add an FMA-polynomial erf: the FMA pipe is the binding one here), per-(image,k) sumsq partials red.add-ed into gsum, fp16 h stores staged through a per-warp 2 KB smem transpose so each STG.128 writes 64 B rows (h_b layout [K2][HW] per image with the two constant rows). Validate pass 1 against a torch reference of the hidden (fp16 tolerance) on a small shape before timing.

STEP 3: the tail (GRN-scale launch + cuBLASLt batched swap-AB GEMM2 exactly as in the notebook recipe), run_tests 16/16 (portal-order re-runs), cuobjdump STACK 0 at <= 128 regs x 512 threads, in-container interleaved x3 vs r9-merge at 64,96 and 32,128, PRECISION LOG over 10 seeded rounds at both rows. Report per-phase stamps (conv-only, pass 1, K3, G2) whatever the outcome: the top-row story needs the numbers even if nothing ships. Success: Conv-only <= 180 us and pass 1 <= 350 us rented at 64,96; rows in-container vs r9-merge 64,96 <= 560 us and 32,128 <= 150 us; run_tests 16/16; precision log 0 beyond own atol on both rows. Refuted if: The conv-only build with bulk-staged row bands and register-blocked patches is > 300 us rented at 64,96 (3x the FMA bound, no better than G's 472 by a margin that pays), or pass 1 with the MMA and GELU warps is > 550 us (the warp roles do not overlap on one SM), in which case the fused top-row family is closed and the remaining top-row lever is the tensor-core Toeplitz conv (I15). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid-barrier counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; cuBLASLt (if any) caches only the per-shape heuristic. No converted weights or other state kept between calls.

task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H45): GEMM2 phase rebuild in tc_kernel: SM-filling unit tables, TMA bulk-reduce epilogue, one-MMA [h|g]. Rows: 2,768 / 8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768 / 8,384 / 16,384 (tc_kernel only; sc rows unchanged). STEP 0 (<=10 min): read the parent card first (what r10 shipped: balanced tables, g or no g, B-scale, KS per row). Run cuobjdump -res-usage on the parent build and record STACK for every tc/sc instantiation (must be 0). Unless the parent card records it done, also run the barrier safety check (audit item 5): protocol review of release/acquire plus fence.proxy.async before any TMA read of data other CTAs wrote with generic stores, and a 1500-call stress loop at 8,768 and 16,384 checked against the torch reference within tolerance. On any failure, revert to cg grid.sync and report. STEP 1: stamp the parent's GEMM2 phase at 8,768, 16,768, 32,768 and 16,384: sync-2 release, first MMA, per-stage time, mainloop end, red.add drain end, units per CTA, busy CTAs. STEP 2 (10-min probe): 148 CTAs, each reduces a 25 KB fp32 smem tile [128 ch][49 tok] (and [128][196]) into a contiguous NCHW fp32 array after the 2xL2 flush. Compare cp.reduce.async.bulk.global.shared::cta.bulk_group.add.f32 (one per image segment, elected thread, commit/wait_group) against the coalesced scalar red.add form. Confirm that ptxas accepts the f32 form on sm_100a, check correctness, and record the time. STEP 3, build: (a) a bulk-reduce epilogue that drains TMEM to smem as dense [c][HW] per image segment and issues one bulk add per segment (prefill out = x + b2' unchanged; handle segments at N padding; wait_group before exit). (b) Per-row unit tables so GEMM2 units are 144-148 (raise KS where units < 120; atomics no longer scale per element). (c) Only if the parent still runs two accumulators with 2N <= 256: land the h and g boxes in adjacent 64-token chunks of one B stage and issue one MMA at 2N (I19). Add (a), (b), (c) one at a time and stamp after each. STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 including portal-order re-runs. Run harness_time interleaved x3 against the parent on the six rows. Check STACK on the shipped build. Precision: only the fp32 summation order of split-K changes, so cite the r8 log plus a single-seed fp64 check per row; if (c) or any B-scale arithmetic changes roundings, log 10 rounds per row. Success: GEMM2 phase (sync-2 release to last CTA exit) at least 40 % shorter on >= 4 of 6 rows. Rows faster than the parent, interleaved x3: 32,768 by >= 4 us, 16,768 and 16,384 by >= 3, 8,768 by >= 2.5, 8,384 by >= 2, 2,768 by >= 1.5. 16/16 pass, STACK 0. Refuted if: The bulk reduce is < 1.3x faster than scalar red.add in STEP 2 AND the shipped build is within 1 us of the parent on >= 4 of 6 rows; or the STEP 1 stamps show the drain is < 1.5 us on every row and filling the SMs gives < 1 us. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid or cluster barrier counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build.

task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H48): sc_kernel: owner-converted resident weights, sync 1 gates only d (seven sc rows). STEP 0, price the chain (<= 5 B200 min). Read the parent card's sc_kernel phase-A order and smem plan in parts. Build two timing-only stubs of sc_kernel; wrong results are allowed and neither is ever shipped. (a) Skip the weight pass and leave the fp16 scratch as garbage; everything else unchanged. (b) As (a), and also skip the post-sync TMA of A, so GEMM1 reads an A image already in smem. Run harness_time interleaved x3 against the parent at 1,192 / 2,96 / 4,192 / 1,160 / 8,192. Take globaltimer stamps of phase-A end and sync-1 release from the working warps. Gate: stub (a) saves >= 1.2 us mean over those rows. If not, stop, record the prices as findings and ship the parent unchanged. STEP 1, GEMM1 weights. At entry each GEMM1 CTA issues cp.async.bulk of its own fp32 W1 rows (128 hidden x C, 98 KB at C=192), beside the plane copies. After its conv units it converts them into its resident SW128 K-major fp16 A image, using the validated address function. In the same pass it computes u_k (rowsum of the rounded fp16(lnw*W1) values) and v_k = W1.lnb + b1. Issue every load before any shuffle, fully unrolled (lesson j). STEP 2, GEMM2 weights. GEMM2 owners bulk-copy their fp32 W2 slice right after sync 1, or at entry if smem allows, and convert it during GEMM1 or the sync-2 wait. b2' = W2.gb + b2 comes from per-K-slice partial sums of the owners; the output reduction is already additive. Reuse raw fp32 landing areas as unit buffers after conversion. If 4,192 / 8,192 exceed 227 KB, convert in two halves through one staging area, or keep the scratch path on those shapes (shape-only dispatch). Keep cg grid.sync on sc_kernel: the flat barrier lost 1-2 us there in r9. STEP 3, checks. cuobjdump -res-usage must show STACK 0 on every sc instantiation. run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs. The u_k summation order changes, so log precision afresh over 10 seeded rounds (seed 200, fp64 reference, harness generators) on all seven sc rows: max |err| and count beyond own atol. The sc class sits at 79-89 % of atol, and any beyond-atol element blocks shipping (fallback: hi/lo split per H22). STEP 4: harness_time interleaved x3 against r11-merge-b on the seven sc rows; record per-row deltas and merge picks. Success: -1.5 us rented or better on at least 5 of the 7 sc rows vs r11-merge-b interleaved x3, 0 beyond-atol elements over 10 rounds, STACK 0 Refuted if: stub (a) saves < 1.2 us mean (the weight chain is already overlapped), or the built version gains < 0.7 us on 4 or more of the 7 rows This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid, cluster or per-image counters (and departure counters) live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value and a per-shape cuBLASLt heuristic; cache hints only on our own workspace buffers; timing-only stubs that skip work must never be the shipped candidate; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build.

task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H49): tc_kernel: GRN scale in the GEMM1 epilogue behind per-image counters, no g, single-accumulator GEMM2. STEP 0 (<= 5 B200 min). Read the parent card in parts to see which tc paths r11-merge-b runs per row: the 7x7 C=768 MP=2 path, the r10 tc2 path on 16,384, and the pair path at B >= 16. Stamp the parent with globaltimer from the working warps; check STACK on the stamp build too. Rows: 32,768 / 16,768 / 8,768 / 16,384. Stamp the GEMM1 per-tile mainloop and the post-accumulator split (pass 1, g pass, stores), the GEMM2 phase and ns per stage, and clk per MMA instruction in the mainloops. Compare the clk with r11 K's straight-line table (N=64 50, N=128 66, N=224 114 clk). If D issues at >= 90 clk per instruction at N <= 128, precomputed descriptors with an unrolled k16 loop may go into the build as a separately stamped change. If the parent card does not record the flat-barrier stress loop, run it now: 1500 calls at 8,768 and 16,384 against the torch reference. Any failure reverts tc_kernel to cg grid.sync. STEP 1, the 7x7 C=768 path. The GEMM1 epilogue keeps the GELU output h in fp32 registers (thread = hidden row, its share of the columns). It reduces the per-(image,k) sumsq inside the CTA and red.adds sum_k gf into a [B] buffer zeroed in phase A. It then release-arrives on a per-image counter, CUTLASS-style: bar.sync, then red.release.gpu from one thread. The expected count is the number of tiles touching image b. Order tiles image-major, and let a CTA wait only after its earlier tiles are done; in the co-resident cooperative grid the wait graph then has no cycle. Spin with ld.acquire, never __nanosleep. Counters self-reset through a departure counter. Then compute inv_b = 1/(mean_k gf + eps) and store h' = fp16(h * (1 + gw*gf*inv_b)) through the staged coalesced store. gb stays in b2'. While the epilogue warps wait, the MMA warp may already issue the CTA's next tile into a second TMEM accumulator. GEMM2 drops g and runs one accumulator over h' alone. Spend the freed stage bytes on more depth, or on MP=2 over h' only, or on 2x tokens per stage, and pick per row. STEP 2: carry the change to the 14x14 paths (on the tc2 path it replaces the in-smem B-scale), to the pair path, and to 2,768 / 8,768. STEP 3: STACK 0 on every instantiation (holding h in registers at N=208 risks spills; split columns over the 4 warps of a quadrant). run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs. h' is new arithmetic, so log precision afresh over 10 rounds (fp64 reference) on every row shipped. Then run harness_time interleaved x3 against r11-merge-b on the six wide-C rows. Stamp the image wait (median and max per tile) and the GEMM2 phase. Success: >= 10 % rented on 32,768 and on 16,768 and >= 5 % on 8,768 vs r11-merge-b interleaved x3; image-wait median <= 1.5 us; 0 beyond-atol elements; STACK 0 Refuted if: < 4 % on both 32,768 and 16,768 after STEP 1, or image-wait median > 2.5 us (per-image skew eats the g saving), or the GEMM2 stage time does not fall without g (stages latency-bound rather than byte- or MMA-bound) This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid, cluster or per-image counters (and departure counters) live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value and a per-shape cuBLASLt heuristic; cache hints only on our own workspace buffers; timing-only stubs that skip work must never be the shipped candidate; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build.

OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid, cluster or per-image counters (and departure counters) live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H24): Post-sync round microbench, then rebuild the cooperative kernel's post-sync loads as single bulk copies with every phase-independent operand prefetched at entry. Step 0 (controls): parent and r0 anchor interleaved x3 under harness_time on all 16 rows; report the clock. Step 1 (microbench, the critic's test, 30 min): a cooperative stub with 296 CTAs that does grid.sync then one per-CTA load round of 6 KB, 12 KB and 32 KB as (a) 4-byte cp.async per element with the parent's index maths, (b) 16-byte cp.async or LDG.128 with every load issued before the first wait, (c) one cp.async.bulk plus one mbarrier wait; the source is (i) lines just written by other CTAs before the sync and (ii) cold DRAM after the 2xL2 flush; stamp globaltimer and clock64 per CTA and report median and max round time and B/clk/SM for each of the 18 cells, plus the grid.sync cost alone with and without pending stores before it. Step 2 (branch on step 1): if (c) is <= 1.2 us for 32 KB just-written, rebuild the flat kernel: one producer warp per CTA with mbarrier full/empty pairs issues at kernel entry the CTA's W1 and W2 fp32 slices (converted with cvt.rn.f16x2 at fragment load, so no weight pass at C<=192), all small vectors in one bulk copy, the residual x tile and the conv halo (3-D TMA box starting at w=-4 with box width W+8, taps offset +1 in smem, as A found; 1-D bulk plane copies for W=7/14); after each grid.sync exactly one bulk or tensor copy per operand (the a/hidden tile, gf); epilogues stage in smem and leave through 16-byte or bulk stores; keep the per-shape templates and the shfl-uniform warp index. If (c) is still >= 2 us but (b) is no better, the cost is post-barrier latency: do not rebuild the loads; instead replace sync2 with per-image counters (self-resetting, zeroed in phase 1 of the same call, ld.acquire.gpu spin with nanosleep) and an image-major tile order (H10 / I16) at 8,192,28,28 and 32,768,7,7, and measure that interleaved x3. Step 3: interleaved A/B against the parent x3 on 1,192; 1,96; 1,160; 2,96; 4,192; 4,96; 8,192; 2,768; set the dispatch per row from that. Step 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check and the per-row max |err| and beyond-own-atol counts over the harness's 10 seeded rounds; apply the hi/lo split where needed. Report the microbench table in the findings whatever the branch taken. Success: Bulk branch: 1,192 <= 22 us and 2,96 <= 32 us rented interleaved (parent 29.8 / 43.4), the other S rows -6 us or more; projected portal >= 0.60. Dataflow branch: >= 6 us faster per row at 8,192 and 32,768. Refuted if: The 32 KB just-written bulk round after a grid.sync costs >= 2 us in the microbench and the rebuilt kernel (either branch) is within 2 us of the parent at 1,192 and 2,96; then the cooperative kernel's floor is barrier-side latency, H24 is refuted, and B's thesis of S rows <= 20 us needs a barrier-free dataflow or should be retired in r4. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

task.instructions: Experiment E3 (tests H25): Weight-stationary cooperative kernel for the six wide-C small-image rows: fp32 weights ingested once per call through TMA/bulk rings, whole-image token tiles with CTA-local GRN statistics, bulk-plane conv. Target rows: 2,768,7,7; 8,768,7,7; 16,768,7,7; 32,768,7,7; 8,384,14,14; 16,384,14,14. The other 10 rows route to the r0 baseline paths through a shape dispatch (correct for all 16). Step 0 (controls): r0 anchor x3 interleaved under harness_time on the six rows; report the clock. Step 1 (stub probe, 30 min, kill gate): a cooperative kernel of <= 148 CTAs that, after the 2xL2 flush, issues at entry a bulk/TMA copy of each CTA's real fp32 W1 and W2 slice bytes (distinct slices, 19 MB total at C=768; 4.7 MB at C=384; TFLOAT32 or FLOAT32 maps, or 1-D cp.async.bulk of contiguous rows), copies 4-channel 7x7 plane groups (784 B) or single 14x14 planes (784 B) with 1-D cp.async.bulk into zero-padded smem planes with all copies issued before any store, does two grid syncs each followed by one bulk load of the real a-tile or hidden-tile size, and red.adds the real GEMM2 partial volume into a prefilled output; harness_time at 2,768 and 32,768. Kill the kernel build if the stub exceeds 20 us at 2,768 or 35 us at 32,768 and spend the rest of the session finding which term is responsible (weight ingest vs post-sync rounds vs red.add) with globaltimer stamps. Step 2: tile table per row with T a multiple of HW (tiles hold whole images) and BN a multiple of 16, e.g. 2,768: T=98, BN=24 (128 CTAs); 8,768: T=196, BN=48; 16,768: T=392, BN=64; 32,768: T=392, BN=96 (4 token tiles x 32 slices = 128 CTAs); 8,384: T=196, BN=64; 16,384: T=392, BN=96; adjust to fit smem (fp32 W1 slice BN*C*4 plus W2 slice C*BN*4, through a ring when above ~100 KB; hidden slice T*BN*2 fp16). Phase A per CTA: bulk-plane conv for its channel share, d written fp16 channel-major to L2 plus per-token LN partial sums, output prefilled with x + b2' (b2' = b2 + gb @ W2^T by spare warps), while a producer warp streams the W1 slice (fp32, resident or ring; convert with cvt.rn.f16x2 at fragment load, never inside the ring); all small vectors bulk-loaded at entry. Sync 1. Phase B: GEMM1 over T tokens x BN hidden with K = C using mma.sync m16n8k16 FP16 (per-shape templates, all fragment LDS first, no runtime guards around HMMA); A = d streamed from L2 in k-chunks; LN applied in the epilogue as r*(acc - mu*s1) + c1 (B's fold); exact erff; hidden slice fp16 kept in smem; per-(image,k) sum of squares is CTA-local because tiles hold whole images, so write gf[b][k] directly and one per-image partial sum over the CTA's k (no atomics). Sync 2. Phase C: read the B x (4C/BN) partial sums (one bulk round), form s_k for the CTA's own channels, scale the smem hidden slice, GEMM2 partial with K = BN against the W2 slice streamed during phase B, red.global.add into the prefilled NCHW output (rows contiguous along hw). Per row decide by arithmetic between red.add split-K (volume M*C*4*(4C/BN) at 4.2 TB/s) and materialising the scaled fp16 hidden in L2 followed by a c-sliced GEMM2 (B's path), and state the choice in the findings. Step 3: interleaved x3 against the r0 anchor on the six rows; globaltimer stamps per phase at 2,768 and 32,768. Step 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check and the per-row max |err| and beyond-own-atol counts over the harness's 10 seeded rounds; apply the hi/lo split where needed. Report the stub table, the tile table, phase stamps and per-row rented times. Success: 2,768 <= 35 us, 8,768 <= 45, 32,768 <= 75 rented (A r2: 64.3 / 63.1 / 97.0; leader-implied 27 / 34 / 67), with 16,768 <= 55 and 8,384 <= 45; run_tests 16/16; the six rows together project >= +0.03 of mean over A r2. Refuted if: The stub in step 1 exceeds 20 us at 2,768 or 35 us at 32,768, or the full kernel is not at least 10 us faster than A r2 at both 2,768 and 8,768 interleaved; then the wide-C rows are bound by post-sync rounds or weight ingest rather than by A's launch chain, and D's thesis moves to a 3-launch TF32 swap-AB specialist (I18) or is retired. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Report per-row rented times with the per-path portal ratio (1.16-1.22 small rows, 1.23-1.32 others) and the projected score. Step 0: parent (v3) and r0 anchor interleaved x3 in your container. GEMM1 epilogue: tcgen05.ld, thread owns hidden channel k and 32 token columns per load; LN fold z = rstd[t]*(acc - mu[t]*u[k]) + v[k] with mu/rstd from smem, exact erff GELU, fp16 hidden to L2 as [k][token] via 16-B stores, per-(image,k) sumsq as in-thread sums (no atomics within a tile; one red.add per (image,k) only if a tile spans a partial image). task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H29): Lineage A lean passes: K2 at stream rate, W2 conversion split over warps, and the owed 10-round precision log. Parent: r4-a-e1-bulkplane-wprep (lineage A's best). Step 0 (hard deliverable, do first): precision log for the parent as shipped, all 16 rows, the harness's 10 seeded rounds (seed 200) against an fp64 reference: per row the max |err| and the count of elements beyond that row's own atol (workload.jsonl) + 1e-5|ref|. If any row has a beyond-atol element, switch its hidden or W2 operand to a hi/lo fp16 split (2 cuBLASLt GEMMs accumulated, or hi/lo columns) and re-log. Step 1 (critic's probe, H29): time K2 alone after the 2xL2 zero-fill at 64,96 / 32,128 / 8,320 against a plain read+write copy kernel of the same fp16 bytes (616 / 134 / 21 MB), interleaved x3; record the copy rate in TB/s. Step 2: rewrite K2 (GELU + GRN sum of squares over the fp16 hidden) as a stream-rate kernel: 256-thread CTAs, each CTA owns a long token run of ONE image (thousands of tokens at 64,96; the whole image at small rows), each thread fixed on 8 hidden channels (one uint4), 8 uint4 loads in flight before the first erff, exact erff kept (a custom erf only if it is at least 1.3x faster AND |err| <= 2e-7 vs erff over [-10,10]), sumsq accumulated in registers across the run, one float4 atomic pair per 8 channels per CTA into the 4-copy accumulators, bias b1 folded as now. Try evict_last on the hidden stores for rows whose hidden is <= 42 MB and evict_first above; keep whichever wins per row class. Keep the kernel sequence identical on every call. Step 3: the W2 conversion in K1 (rows with the hidden > 16 MB: B >= 8 at C=768, B = 16 at C=384) is one warp per W2 row with 4 serial 768-column rounds: split each row over 4 warps with a CTA-level reduction and 16-B loads, all loads issued before use; target weights-only K1 <= 6 us at C=768 (now 8.9-11), measured with the conv-only / weights-only / both ablation at 2,768, 8,768, 16,768. Step 4: run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds with the parent interleaved x3 in the same container as the control, and the r0 anchor once for the ratio; report per-row rented deltas, not band means. Step 5 (optional if time remains): the nwmin 4 vs 8 interleaved comparison left open in r4. Report findings with sources; a session that ends without the step 0 log returns no candidate. Success: K2 at 64,96 <= 260 us rented (from 447), 32,128 <= 65 (from 113), 8,320 <= 22 (from 38), so the full rows reach 64,96 <= 960, 32,128 <= 245, 8,320 <= 75 rented against the parent in the same container; weights-only K1 <= 6 us at C=768 with 8,768 and 16,768 gaining >= 3 us; precision log delivered with 0 beyond-atol elements on all 16 rows (or the hi/lo fix applied where needed). Refuted if: The copy probe shows the parent's K2 already at >= 80% of the copy kernel's rate at 64,96 (then the kernel is SIMT-bound and only a cheaper erf helps), or the rewritten K2 is within 15% of the old one at 64,96 and 32,128 in the same container. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE: cache hints (evict_last/evict_first, applypriority) only on this kernel's own scratch buffers, never on the harness's inputs or output.

task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H30): New lineage E: CUTLASS sm100 builder GEMMs with EVT fusion and TF32 operands straight from fp32 memory for the six wide-C small-image rows. Build from scratch (you may read only the r0 anchor and the lineage conclusions; do not read lineage A/B/D code). Target rows: 2,768,7,7; 8,768,7,7; 16,768,7,7; 32,768,7,7; 8,384,14,14; 16,384,14,14. All other rows run the r0 anchor path unchanged (the operator merges per workload). Language 'cutlass' (C++; two files: kernel.cu with no torch headers plus binding.cpp; CUTLASS 4.4.1 headers at $CUTLASS_DIR/include; target_hardware [B200] only, since tcgen05 code does not build for plain sm_100). Pipeline per call, 4-5 launches: (K1) your own bulk-plane depthwise conv for 7x7/14x14 images: 1-D cp.async.bulk of channel-plane groups into zero-padded smem, one thread per 7-output row segment, plus the dwconv bias; write d as fp32 TOKEN-MAJOR [b][hw][C] (tcgen05 kind::tf32 needs K-major A and B), per-token LN partial sums (sum, sumsq) via atomics or per-group partials finalised as mu[token], rstd[token]; spare CTAs compute the fold vectors u[n] = sum_c W1[n][c]*lnw[c], v[n] = sum_c W1[n][c]*lnb[c] + b1[n] and b2'[c] = sum_k W2[c][k]*gb[k] + b2[c] (coalesced 16-B loads, all loads issued before use, compile-time trip counts). No weight conversion in the first build: both GEMMs use TF32. (G1) CUTLASS CollectiveBuilder, arch Sm100, KernelTmaWarpSpecialized1SmSm100 (or 2Sm where the tile allows), batched L = B images, M = HW (49 or 196, tile M = 64 or 128), N = 4C, K = C; ElementA = ElementB = cutlass::tfloat32_t on the fp32 d and fp32 W1 (verify in step 1 that the resulting TMA descriptor uses the TFLOAT32 data type: compare one tile's accumulator against an fp64 reference of round-to-nearest TF32 operands and against truncation; the bit pattern must match RNE, H14). EVT epilogue: Sm90RowBroadcast(rstd, mu with batch stride), Sm90ColBroadcast(u, v), compute z = rstd*(acc - mu*u) + v, cutlass::epilogue::thread::GELU (the erf form, NOT GELU_taylor), store the hidden (fp32 for the TF32 rows, [b][hw][4C] K-major for GEMM2) and Sm90ColReduction of z*z over M per batch into gf2[b][k] (atomic across M tiles where M > tile). If the sm100 epilogue cannot instantiate the ColReduction, fall back to an AuxStore of the hidden and compute the per-image sumsq in K3 with a cluster of 8 CTAs per image exchanging the 4C partials through DSMEM. (K3) one-round GRN scale kernel: grid (image, k-slice), each CTA reads gf2[b][:] (12 KB), computes gf = sqrt, mean_k, s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*gf/(mean+eps), then rescales its hidden slice in place with all loads issued before any store; nothing else is chained. (G2) CUTLASS batched: A = W2 [C][4C] (tf32, batch stride 0), B = scaled hidden [hw][4C] per image (K-major, N = HW), D[b][c][hw] with batch stride C*HW = NCHW directly, source C = x (beta = 1) and per-row bias b2'. The CTA count is tiny at 7x7 (6*B tiles), so use split-K: first try the sm100 stream-K/split-K scheduler; if it is not available in 4.4.1, run batched over (image, k-split) with fp32 partials [B*KS][C][HW] and a one-round reduce+residual kernel (coalesced, all loads first). Steps: (0) time the r0 anchor interleaved x3 as the in-session control; (1) compile gate with no GPU needed first: G1 and G2 instantiations for 49x3072x768 (L=8) and 196x1536x384 (L=8), record nvcc wall time (abort the design if two instantiations exceed 200 s: the portal limit is 300 s), registers, smem, spills; then the H14 bit check; (2) time G1 cold (after a 2xL2 zero-fill) at 8,768 and 8,384 and compare with the leader-implied budget: kill the EVT route if G1 alone exceeds 14 us at 8,768 (that is cuBLASLt GEMM1 + K2 on lineage A); (3) full pipeline, run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds with the portal-order check; (4) precision log on the six rows: 10 seeded rounds (seed 200) vs an fp64 reference, per row max |err| and count beyond atol + 1e-5|ref| (TF32 RNE is the same 10-bit mantissa as fp16, so expect max about 2.4e-3 at 32,768; any beyond-atol element switches that row's activation operand to an fp16 hi/lo split or fp32 SIMT); (5) per-launch cold breakdown (harness_time) of K1/G1/K3/G2 on 8,768 and 8,384, and if GEMM2 is ingest-bound at low CTA counts (H31), raise KS. Report every finding with its source, including compile times and which EVT nodes instantiated. Success: run_tests 16/16; the six target rows at or under 2,768 32 / 8,768 38 / 8,384 42 / 16,384 58 / 16,768 50 / 32,768 68 us rented on at least 4 of 6 rows, with the parent-equivalent merge rows timed in the same container (operator-provided numbers: A r4 48.5 / 44.4 / 50.4 / 71.5 / 53.2 / 70.1, D r4 32.4 at 2,768); CUTLASS build time under 200 s; precision log delivered with 0 beyond-atol elements. Refuted if: G1 with the EVT epilogue runs slower cold than 14 us at 8,768 or 12 us at 8,384 (then the library epilogue is no cheaper than cuBLASLt + K2), or the per-batch column reduction and the split-K GEMM2 both fail to instantiate on sm100 and the fallbacks push the six rows above A's times, or the build exceeds 200 s. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules for the CUTLASS route): (1) no PDL anywhere: launch every CUTLASS kernel without programmatic dependent launch (GemmUniversalAdapter::run / operator() with launch_with_pdl left false; never set cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization). (2) Call the adapter's initialize() (or to_underlying_arguments) with this call's pointers on every call: its params embed TMA descriptors, which must be encoded per call; cache only shape-keyed configuration, never an initialised Gemm object or converted data. (3) The CUTLASS workspace and every atomic accumulator (gf2, LN partials, split-K partials) come from torch.empty inside run(), which is uninitialised: zero them with your own kernel or cudaMemsetAsync on the current stream in every call before use. (4) Spec language may be 'cutlass' or 'cuda_cpp' (both compile the same way); keep ld_flags you need (e.g. -lcuda).

hypothesis: >-
  Lineage D / E2 (H33). Stamping showed that the r4 tcgen05 kernel's roughly 2x excess on 32,768 and the 14x14 rows
  was the GEMM1 epilogue (45-49 us per tile), not operand ingest. Its hreg[4][16] array lived in local memory:
  128 B stack and 35-36 LDL/STL per instance, with L1 squeezed by 227 KB of smem. Changes:
  (1) a register-only epilogue (no per-thread arrays, 112-118 regs, 0 stack);
  (2) h stored through a per-warp smem transpose, so 4 lanes write each 64-B row segment, and g = fp16(gw*gf*h) made
  by each thread re-reading its own L2-hot h;
  (3) phase-A weight work split into 8C equal C-float units (W1 rows plus W2 quarter rows with partial W2.gb), handed
  out from the highest CTA down;
  (4) a float4 red.add GEMM2 epilogue at 14x14.
  The engine stays 1SM. The cta_group::2 probe reaches the MMA ideal, but the port is deferred.

  S: {pct: 0, confidence: high}
  M: {pct: -30, confidence: medium}
  L: {pct: -10, confidence: medium}

findings:
