task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H33): D: stamp the 2x at 32,768 / 14x14 rows, then cta_group::2 pairs or B multicast to lift the operand-ingest bound of the swap-AB tcgen05 engine. STEP 0: run_tests r4-d-tc05-swapab and the r0 anchor interleaved x3 in this container to set the session baseline (cross-host drift is 5-12 us). Deliver the owed precision log: fp64 reference, 10 seeded rounds from seed 200 with the harness generators, per row max |err| and beyond-own-atol count, for the r4 paths on the six wide-C rows and for the r3-ws-coop-widec path at 2,768 (the merge ships it). STEP 1: globaltimer stamps (CTA medians and max) at phase A end, sync 1, GEMM1 mainloop end, GEMM1 epilogue end, sync 2, GEMM2 mainloop end, red end, at 32,768, 16,384, 8,384 and 8,768; identify which term carries the ~2x above the 40-50 us bytes-and-ingest estimate (suspects: GEMM1 epilogue issue rate, doubled GEMM2 B ingest from g, scalar red volume, 2 tiles per CTA). STEP 2, ingest probe on the r4 gate GEMM (128xNT swap-AB tile, SW128 TMA ring, warm L2, clk per 64-k stage, N = 112 / 128 / 224, K = 768 and 3072, 148 CTAs): (a) 1SM as r4; (b) cta_group::2 pair: cluster 2x1, M = 256 across the pair (each CTA its 128 rows of the weight tile), each CTA loads half of the B token tile into its own smem, the even CTA issues the MMA with the pair descriptors, tcgen05.commit with the multicast form to both CTAs' barriers, consumer release through the cluster-scope barrier; (c) 1SM with the B tile TMA-multicast across a cluster of two CTAs that hold different weight tiles. Report clk per stage vs the MMA ideal (2N clk) for each; go with the variant at <= 1.3x the ideal; also record which of (b) and (c) wins, because that tells whether the H31 cap is SM-side or L2-side. STEP 3: port the winner into GEMM1 and GEMM2 of the cooperative kernel, keeping the cooperative launch, the validated descriptors (MN-major SW128 B: LBO 8192, SBO 1024; +2048 per k16), the bulk-plane conv and the CTA-local statistics; pair tiles must keep tile counts a multiple of 74 pairs per row (pick N and split-K per row). Fix the largest stamped term from step 1 (epilogue: 2 rows x 16 columns per lane with every tcgen05.ld issued first; red: red.global.add.v4 instead of scalar; B ingest: per-K-row s_b transform on the B stage instead of the g accumulator if the doubled ingest is the term). STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, interleaved with the parent and the r0 anchor; report per row rented times, the stamps before and after, and the per-stage clk. Reminder: target_hardware [B200] only; a release arrive from a warp with loads in flight stalls (tricks s5); clusters are allowed here because the GEMM tile needs them. Success: Per-64-k stage <= 1.3x the MMA ideal in the probe, and the full kernel at least 8 us under A r5 on three or more of 8,768 (48.1), 16,768 (56.1), 32,768 (70.2), 8,384 (50.2), 16,384 (62.1), with 2,768 <= 32 kept and 0 beyond-own-atol elements over 10 seeded rounds on the six rows. Refuted if: Both the pair and the multicast variant stay above 1.5x the MMA ideal per stage (then the ingest cap is not operand-bytes-per-SM and a wide-C single-launch design must reuse weight tiles from smem across all tokens instead), or the ported kernel is not >= 8 us faster than A r5 on any of the five rows. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE: the globaltimer stamps are diagnostics: compile them out of (or leave them disabled by default in) the shipped kernel so the timed path writes no stamp buffer.

task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H32): New design: library-lean four-launch pipeline (LN in K1 via cluster DSMEM stats, cuBLASLt GELU epilogue, one-launch GRN scale, swap-AB NCHW GEMM2 with residual, L2 weight prefetch). Build from scratch (you may read the r0 baseline r0-convnext-coop-fp32-anchor for host plumbing and the per-lineage conclusions for recipes; no other lineage code). Target rows in order: the six wide-C rows (2,768; 8,768; 16,768; 32,768; 8,384; 16,384), then the HW=784 rows (1,192; 4,192; 8,192), then 1,160,449,7, then 1,96 / 2,96 if time allows. Rows you do not reach run a simple correct fallback (the r0 baseline path is acceptable); the merge keeps A there. CUDA C++ two-file layout (kernel.cu without torch headers, binding.cpp), cuBLASLt from the binding, one handle and per-shape plans set up on first use and valid in any shape order. STEP 0, kill gates, cold after a 2xL2 zero-fill, harness_time x3, interleave the r0 anchor: (a) cuBLASLt fp16 GEMM1 [M x C]x[C x 4C] with CUBLASLT_EPILOGUE_GELU_BIAS (fp16 out, fp32 compute) vs EPILOGUE_BIAS at 392x3072x768, 1568x1536x384, 784x768x192: the GELU delta must be <= 1.5 us per shape (kill at > 3 us on two shapes). (b) GEMM2 in the swap-AB batched form: per image b, D_b[C x HW] = W2[C x 4C] * h_b^T (h_b fp16 [HW x 4C] row-major, so op(B) = T), beta = 1 with C_b = x_b (fp32 [C x HW], the NCHW slab) and a per-row bias b2' = W2*gb + b2 through EPILOGUE_BIAS, strided batch over images (B = 2..32, N = 49 / 196 / 784): time it against channels-last GEMM2 plus a 32x32 transpose-add kernel at 8,768, 8,384, 1,192; adopt swap-AB where it is <= channels-last + 3 us, else keep the transpose-add (5 launches on those rows). (c) A 4-launch stub (each kernel one dependent L2 round of the real bytes) to record the launch floor on this host. STEP 1, K1: 1-D cp.async.bulk plane copies into zero-padded smem (plane groups 16-B aligned; per-lane copies rounded outward to 16 B for 49-float planes; bank-skew slots for odd HW), one thread per 7-output row segment, 49 taps and bias in registers, per-token (sum, sumsq) partials; grid = (image, row strip) x cluster of 8 CTAs along channels (C/8 channels each: 96 at C=768, 48 at C=384, 24 at C=192, 20 at C=160); exchange the 2 floats per token through DSMEM (cluster barrier, each CTA reads the 7 peers' partials), then apply LayerNorm with lnw/lnb in-CTA and write a16 token-major [M][C] fp16 (or the channel-major TT layout if cuBLASLt's heuristic prefers it; test both at 8,768). Role CTAs (or a first round over all CTAs, all loads issued before use) convert W1 and W2 to fp16 with 16-B loads/stores, compute b2' in fp32 (hi/lo fp16 columns not needed since the bias is applied in fp32 by the epilogue), and issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 of the fp32 W1/W2 at entry so the conversion reads hit L2 (I26). Also build a no-cluster control of K1 (d16 + stats, no LN) to isolate the cluster cost; report both. STEP 2, G1 per step 0a. STEP 3, K3': grid = B x (4C/KS) CTAs with KS = 256 (128 at C<=192), each reads its HW x KS fp16 slice (all tokens of its image) from L2 with every load issued first, column sumsq -> gf[k] = sqrt, red.add of its sum_k gf into a per-image fp32 cell plus a red.release arrival counter in a torch.empty int32 workspace with a generation word (self-resetting: the last arriver clears the cell and bumps the generation; correct for every call and shape order), spins with ld.acquire until the image's 4C/KS CTAs have arrived, computes s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*gf[k]/(mean + eps), rescales its slice in place (fp16) and adds gb[k] where the gb term is not folded into b2' (fold it: h' = h*s_b, bias b2' = W2*gb + b2). Co-residency: check with cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor that the grid fits in one wave (max 32x12 = 384 CTAs at 32,768) else launch cooperatively. STEP 4, G2 per step 0b. STEP 5, precision log, mandatory: fp64 reference, 10 seeded rounds from seed 200 with the harness generators, per row max |err| and the count beyond that row's own atol + 1e-5|ref|, for every path you ship (a16 is one fp16 rounding of a ~N(0,1) value, hidden one rounding, W1/W2 one rounding each). STEP 6, run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, interleaved with the r0 anchor; report per row rented time and launch count, and the step 0 probe numbers. Report what was not done. Success: Four launches on the wide-C rows (five if the transpose-add stays) and rented times at least 8 us under A r5 (8,768 48.1; 8,384 50.2; 16,384 62.1; 16,768 56.1; 32,768 70.2; 2,768 54.5) on three or more of the six rows, with 0 beyond-own-atol elements over the 10 seeded rounds on every shipped row; stretch: 1,192 <= 28, 4,192 <= 32, 8,192 <= 44 rented. Refuted if: The cuBLASLt GELU_BIAS epilogue costs > 3 us over BIAS at both 8,768 and 8,384 shapes (then the library epilogue route is dead and the finding goes to the pool), or the full four-launch pipeline is within 3 us of A r5 on all six wide-C rows in the same container. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (1) The K3' arrival counter and generation word must NOT live in torch.empty memory: it is uninitialised and can hold any earlier tensor's bytes (tests pass by luck, the portal deadlocks). Put them in a module-level __device__ buffer zero-initialised at load, sized for the largest grid, and have the last arriver reset it, so every call and every shape order starts from zero. (2) cuBLASLt plans are shape-keyed, but the bias / epilogue pointers stored on a matmul descriptor (CUBLASLT_MATMUL_DESC_BIAS_POINTER etc.) change every call: set them on every call, never reuse a pointer from an earlier call. (3) cuBLASLt's GELU epilogue may be the tanh approximation of GELU: allowed only if the step 5 precision log is clean on every row that uses it; the tightest current row (1,96) already sits at 90% of its atol with the fp16 path, so log every shipped row.

task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H34): Port D's single-launch tcgen05 skeleton to the lowest-scoring S/M rows: 1,192 / 4,192 / 8,192 (28x28), 2,96 (56x56) and 1,160 (449x7), wide-C rows unchanged. Keep the six wide-C rows on the r6 code path bit-identical (same tile tables); add a small-C path and a shape dispatch; rows not covered run the r0 fallback (merge-only candidate). STEP 0: interleave r6-merge in your container as the control (its paths: B coop at 1,192 29.5-30.8 rented, A r5 at 4,192 34.0, 8,192 46.1, 2,96 36.8, 1,160 39.6) and stamp the r6 kernel at 2,768 with globaltimer from the working warps (phase A end, sync 1 release, GEMM1 mainloop end, GEMM1 epilogue end, sync 2 release, GEMM2 end, red end): that is the chain budget the small-C rows inherit (27.6 us with phase A 7.4). STEP 1, conv: bulk-plane units for 28x28 planes (3136 B, 16-B multiple; 32 planes = 100 KB per unit, thread per 7-output row segment: 4 segments x 28 rows = 112 threads per plane) and 56x56 planes (12544 B; 8 planes per unit with zero-padded 62x62 slots, 8 segments x 56 rows = 448 threads per plane); for 449x7 the planes are 12572 B (not a multiple of 16): bulk-copy the 16-B-aligned superset [align_down(start), align_up(end)) into a slot and read the conv input at offset (start mod 16) bytes; W=7 rows use whole-row strips with compile-time tap masks. Per-token LN sum/sumsq across channel units as the r6 code does for 7x7 (atomics or a per-token second pass); the fp16 weight conversion (W1' = lnw-folded W1 and u, W2, b2' = W2.gb + b2) spread over all CTAs as one pass (1.2 MB at C=192); out prefilled with x + b2' in phase A where split-K is used. STEP 2, GEMM1 tiles: swap-AB A = 128 hidden-row tiles of W1' (6 at C=192, 3 at C=96, 5 at C=160), B = d16 [C][N tokens] MN-major SW128, N = 112 or 128-token chunks of one image (784 = 7 x 112; 3136 = 28 x 112; 3143 -> 29 x 112 with the last chunk padded, pad columns masked out of the sumsq as the HWS padding is today); per-(image,k) sumsq by one red.global.add.f32 per (image,k) per tile since chunks of one image now span tiles; persistent loop over tiles (42 / 168 / 336 / 168 / 145 tiles). Keep the epilogue register-resident (check cuobjdump STACK = 0) and size N so that the per-tile post-accumulator phase is <= 2 us. STEP 3, GEMM2: M = C as a 128-row tile plus a 64-row tile at C=192 (UMMA M=64 is legal for 1SM; or 128 with masking), M=96 -> 128 padded at C=96, M=160 -> 128 + 32-padded-to-64 at C=160; N = the same token chunks; K = 4C split KS so that CTA count >= 148 with k-slices of >= 128 (1,192: 2 x 7 x KS); keep the two-accumulator (h and g) GRN form; coalesced red.global.add.v4 into the prefilled output, which is NCHW-natural because the tile is [c][tokens] with tokens contiguous per image row... for 28x28 and 56x56 images the token index is h*W + w, so the [c][token] tile maps straight onto x[b][c][:, :] rows. STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 (portal-order check), interleaved x3 with r6-merge; report per-row times, the stamps at 1,192 and 2,768, and the wide-C rows unchanged within noise. STEP 5: precision log (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds) for every new path (max |err|, beyond-own-atol count; 1,192 has the tightest atol 2.4e-3). Also log the B paths of r6-merge (1,192; 1,96) if time allows, since they are owed. Do not start the cta_group::2 pair port in this session; if the small-C port finishes early, use the time to stamp and shrink the 1,192 chain (dependent rounds after each sync, conv tail). Success: run_tests 16/16; 1,192 <= 24 us rented and at least 4 us under the r6-merge path on 3 of the 5 target rows (1,192; 4,192; 8,192; 2,96; 1,160) in the same container; wide-C rows within 1 us of r6-d-e2-epi-fix; 0 beyond-own-atol elements over 10 seeded rounds on every new path. Refuted if: 1,192 >= 28 us rented (no better than B's 29.5-30.8 within noise) with stamps showing the time is sync releases plus dependent rounds rather than removable phase work, or fewer than 2 of the 5 target rows beat the merge path by >= 2 us. Then the single-launch route for S rows is closed and B stays paused. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every new red.add / atomic target (per-(image,k) sumsq across tiles, split-K output) must be zeroed or prefilled inside the launch before the grid sync that precedes its first use, as r6 does for gsum; the workspace is torch.empty (uninitialised). Stamps compiled out of the shipped build.

task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H35): Fused conv -> tcgen05 GEMM1 -> exact GELU -> GRN stats pass for the HW >= 1024 rows (64,96; 32,128; 8,320), plus GRN-scale launch and batched swap-AB cuBLASLt GEMM2 writing NCHW. Rows: 64,96,112,112 and 32,128,64,64 first, 8,320,32,32 and 4,96,56,56 as stretch; every other row runs the r0 fallback (merge-only candidate). Lineage isolation: you may read only the r0 baseline; the notebook holds the validated tcgen05 facts you need (r6 D: MN-major SW128 B descriptor LBO 8192 / SBO 1024 / +2048 per k16, instruction-descriptor bits, 1SM landing cap 68-92 B/clk/SM, per-stage floor ~480 clk at N=128, STACK-frame pitfall, stamps only from working warps; r2 A: TMA 3-D box inner start must be a multiple of 16 B, so start the halo box at w=-4 with width W+8). STEP 0 (gate, <= 1/4 of the session): a single-CTA fused tile for the 64,96 geometry. 4-8 conv warps consume a TMA 3-D box ring of x over channel groups of 16-32 (tile = 2 or 4 image rows x 112 columns plus the 6-row halo; try 4 rows if smem allows, it halves the staging redundancy), compute the 7x7 depthwise conv with the 49 taps in registers and per-token sum/sumsq, and write fp16 d as [c][token] into a 128B-swizzled smem B tile (C x 224 or 448 tokens). One MMA warp runs kind::f16 128 x N x 96 for each of the 3 hidden M-tiles with W1' (384 x 96 fp16 = 74 KB, folded with lnw) resident in smem, two TMEM accumulators ping-pong (2 x 224 columns). 4 epilogue warps: tcgen05.ld, LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u[k]) + v[k] (lane = k, per-token mu/rs from smem), exact erf GELU where half of each thread's elements use an FMA-only minimax odd polynomial (|err| <= 5e-7 on [-4,4], clamped beyond) and half the ex2/rcp A&S-style form, square-accumulate per (image,k) in registers, fp16 h stores staged through smem for 16-B coalesced [k][token] or [token][k] writes (pick the layout GEMM2 wants). Validate the tile against torch (fp32 reference, max err <= 2e-5 before fp16 rounding of h; the erf forms against erff to 5e-7). Measure clk per tile for conv-only, epilogue-only, MMA-only and full; the SIMT bound per 224-token tile is ~8.2k clk conv + ~13.4k clk GELU (20 instr/element) or ~7k with the balanced erf. GO if the full tile is <= 1.5x (conv + epilogue) bound; if it is >= 2x, stop and report where the cycles go (LDS, issue, TMEM loads). If the tcgen05 descriptor work is not correct after 1/3 of the session, fall back to mma.sync m16n8k16 for GEMM1 in the same fused structure (the hypothesis is the fusion, not the engine; mma.sync costs ~130 us of tensor time at 64,96 that overlaps the SIMT work). STEP 1: persistent pass-1 kernel (1 CTA/SM, 148 CTAs, static tile loop over (image, row-block) tiles; per-(image,k) sumsq via one red.global.add.f32 per tile per k; hidden fp16 to a torch.empty scratch; stamps from the working warps for conv wait, MMA, epilogue per tile). At C=128 (32,128) W1' is 128 KB: stream it per M-tile through a TMA ring (32 KB per 128 x 128 tile) or hold two of the four M-tiles; at C=320 (8,320) stream it. STEP 2: pass 2. K3' = one plain launch: per image s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k] * gf[b][k] / (mean_k gf[b] + eps) from the sums, fp16 W2_b = fp16(W2 * s_b) per image (C x 4C per image: 74 KB at C=96, 4.7 MB total at 64,96), b2' = W2.gb + b2 in fp32 as hi/lo fp16 K-augmentation columns or an fp32 bias; then cuBLASLt batched swap-AB GEMM2: D_b[C x HW] = W2_b * h_b^T + x_b (C operand = x_b, beta 1, batch = images, fp32 D written straight into the NCHW output). F found this form 2-4 us faster than channels-last + transpose at HW=784 and fine above; if cuBLASLt picks a slow kernel for 64 batches, fall back to channels-last GEMM2 plus a transpose-add kernel. Three launches total. STEP 3: run_tests all 16 rows (portal-order check), interleaved x3 with r6-merge in the same container (that is the control: A r5 1027 / 259 / 78.6 us at 64,96 / 32,128 / 8,320). Report per-launch times (pass 1, K3', GEMM2) and the pass-1 stamps. STEP 4: precision log (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds) for every shipped row: max |err| and beyond-own-atol count; roundings are d16, fp16(W1'), h16, fp16(W2_b): the same set A ships, plus the per-image W2 scaling, which rounds s_b*W2 once (relative 2^-11, same as fp16(W2)). Record SASS STACK/LDL counts for the pass-1 kernel. Record findings in the card: tile clk breakdown, erf split speed vs erff, staging redundancy chosen, cuBLASLt batched G2 time at 64 and 32 batches. Success: run_tests 16/16 with the gate met; 64,96 <= 750 us and 32,128 <= 190 us rented in the same container as r6-merge (1027 / 259), pass 1 alone <= 450 / 110 us, 0 beyond-own-atol elements over 10 seeded rounds on every shipped row. Stretch: 8,320 <= 60. Refuted if: The gate tile runs >= 2x the SIMT bound with no identified removable term, or pass 1 alone is >= K1 + G1 + K2 of A (825 us at 64,96 or 205 at 32,128) in the same container, or any shipped row has a beyond-atol element that the hi/lo split of W2_b does not fix. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (1) torch.empty memory is uninitialised: the per-(image,k) sumsq accumulators (and any other red.add target) must be zeroed in this call before the first red.add (a zero pass inside an earlier kernel of this call, cudaMemsetAsync on the current stream, or per-tile partials reduced in K3' with no atomics); never rely on a previous call's state. (2) cuBLASLt plans may be shape-keyed, but every pointer on a matmul descriptor (bias, epilogue aux) and the batched pointers/strides must be set on every call. (3) No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build (the timed path writes no stamp buffer).

STEP 0 (<= 8 B200 min): add 4,96,56,56 to sc_kernel's dispatch table (the C=96 56x56 instantiation exists; B=4 only changes the tile table) and, if the C=320 32x32 instantiation compiles without new code paths (4096-B planes, 4C = 1280 = 20 N-chunks of 64, 5 K-blocks), 8,320 too; run_tests with r7-merge as the same-container control; keep each row only if it beats the merge path by >= 2 us rented. STEP 1 (stamps): TC_STAMPS on tc_kernel at 16,384 and 8,384 from the epilogue warps (per-tile post-accumulator time, expected 11.7 / 10.9 us) and on sc_kernel at 8,192 (3 x 3.9 us); record them as the baseline. STEP 2 (the experiment): after the accumulator-full barrier of each GEMM1 tile, run the epilogue on every warp of the CTA (12 now; go to 16 warps / 512 threads if registers stay <= 128 with STACK 0): warp w serves TMEM lanes 32*(w%4)..+31 and the column slice (w/4) of the tile, each thread keeps two tcgen05.ld of 16-32 columns in flight, applies the LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + v, the A&S erfc GELU (the form used by G r7 and A r5, |err| <= 1.2e-6 in h), accumulates its per-(image,k) sumsq partial in registers and combines partials across the column-slice warps through smem (one value per lane per quadrant) before the existing red.add / store; keep the staged coalesced h stores. Check cuobjdump: STACK 0, no LDL/STL, registers; stamp again at the same rows. STEP 3: interleaved x3 vs the parent in one container (harness_time) at 16,384 / 8,384 / 32,768 / 8,768 / 4,192 / 8,192. STEP 4 (stretch, only if >= 15 B200 min remain): port the r6 cta_group::2 recipe to GEMM2 (cluster 2x1, each CTA loads half of the B token tile, leader-only MMA, multicast commit) and measure the GEMM2 wait / B-tile scale term at 8,192 and 8,768. STEP 5: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, and the PRECISION LOG (fp64 reference, harness generators, torch.manual_seed(200), 10 rounds, max |err| and beyond-own-atol count) for every changed path (all 12 rows). Report per-row rented times vs the parent, the per-tile epilogue before/after, registers, and which rows the merge should take. Success: In one container vs the parent: per-tile post-accumulator epilogue down >= 40 % at 16,384 and 8,384; rows 16,384 <= 48, 8,384 <= 32, 32,768 <= 58 us rented (D takes 32,768 from A), no row slower than the parent by > 1 us; 16/16 pass; 0 beyond-own-atol on every changed path. Refuted if: Doubling the epilogue warps cuts the per-tile post-accumulator time by < 25 % with STACK 0 and no spills: then the epilogue is bound by TMEM-load or store latency per warp, not by warp count, and the next lever is restructuring the loads (report the stamps and the SASS mix). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) every red.add / atomic target, old or new (gsq per (image,k), split-K output), must be zeroed or prefilled inside the launch before the grid sync that precedes its first use, as r6/r7 do; the workspace is torch.empty (uninitialised). (b) TMA descriptors encoded on every call, as now. (c) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes/plans.

  for the two missing HW >= 1024 rows. Each CTA takes one 2-row tile and all 16 warps work through it in order.
  4,96 uses 112-token tiles padded to 128 (112 CTAs) with W1' resident in shared memory. 8,320 uses 64-token tiles

  - "Per-tile stamps (globaltimer, flush, CTA median/max from kernel start; tid 0 / warp 0), 4,96 shipped: prologue 0.5, conv end 9.2/10.2, stats end 10.0/11.0, GEMM end 18.7/19.5 us; warp 0 GEMM side mma 3.3 us + epilogue 4.5 us for 2 warp tiles; W1' wait 0.05 us. 8,320: conv end 12.8/13.8, stats 14.1/14.9, end 39.7/41.0; warp 0 ring wait 0.34, mma 16.2, epilogue 8.4 us over 5 blocks (clock 1.78-1.88 GHz) [probe_b200]"

  - "Merge recommendation: take 4,96 and 8,320 from this kernel (4 launches each vs A's 5-6, so the portal ratio should be no worse than A's 1.23-1.30); keep 64,96 / 32,128 from r7 G (identical code). Rough portal: 4,96 37 x 1.27 = 47 us vs 57.4; 8,320 67 x 1.27 = 85 us vs 99.7 [INFERRED]"

task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H37): Fused pass-1 pipeline instantiated for 8,320 (streamed W1', 64-token tiles) and 4,96 (112-token tiles with a masked warp tile). Rows 8,320,32,32 and 4,96,56,56 only; the 64,96 / 32,128 paths stay as shipped and must time within noise of the parent. STEP 1, 4,96: tiles of R=2 image rows = 112 tokens padded to 128 (four 32-token warp tiles, the fourth half-masked: zero the padded d columns and skip their stores and sumsq), 112 CTAs; W1' (74 KB) resident as at 64,96; reuse the 56x56 TMA halo staging. Time pass 1, K3 and the batched swap-AB cuBLASLt GEMM2 (7.3 us measured at 4 batches); compare with the merge path (A, 46.8 rented in r7's container) interleaved x3. STEP 2, 8,320: C=320 makes W1' 819 KB, so stream it per 128-hidden-row block (80 KB fp16 per block, 10 blocks) through a double-buffered cp.async.bulk ring from the fp16 W1' scratch written by K0, double-buffered against the mma loop; d tile 64 tokens x 320 channels fp16 (40 KB); try R=2 (64-token tiles, 128 CTAs) first and R=1 (32-token tiles, 256 items, 2 per CTA) if the per-tile chain is latency-bound; GEMM2 batched swap-AB at HW=1024 with 8 batches (check the heuristic kernel and time it cold). Stamp pass 1 per tile (ingest wait, mma, GELU, stores) from the working warps. STEP 3: run_tests 16/16 (portal-order check) with r7-merge as the same-container control; PRECISION LOG (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds) for both new rows. STEP 4 (stretch, only if >= 12 B200 min remain): the balanced erf (I30): route one third of the elements through an FMA-only minimax erf polynomial (|err| <= 5e-7, clamped) and measure the GEMM side alone at 64,96 and 32,128. Report per-row rented times, the per-tile stamps, registers/smem per instantiation, and which rows the merge should take. Success: In one container vs r7-merge: 4,96 <= 36 us rented (merge path 46.8) and 8,320 <= 55 us (78.6), 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-own-atol on both rows, the two large rows unchanged within 2 %. Refuted if: 4,96 with 112 tiles is not faster than the merge path, or 8,320 pass 1 exceeds 45 us with the W1' ring stamped as overlapped (then the serial per-tile chain, not SM count, binds and the fused structure does not transfer to C >= 320). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) the GRN sums and any new red.add target must be zeroed by K0 in the same call (as r7 does); the fp16 W1' scratch for the 8,320 ring is written by K0 in the same call, never kept from an earlier call. (b) cuBLASLt: only the heuristic result may be cached per shape; descriptors, batch strides and pointers set on every call, as r7 does. (c) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes/plans.

r8-h-dataflow-queue.card:
id: r8-h-dataflow-queue
parents: [r0-convnext-coop-fp32-anchor]
operation: new_design
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: tma-tensor
  st: direct
  grid: persistent
  launch: fused
  tile: rows128
  red: cta
  cache: default
  spec: dispatch:size
hypothesis: >-
  H38 (lineage H, E3): one cooperative persistent tcgen05 kernel, 148 CTAs with 256 threads each, works through a static queue
  [W1 units][conv units][GEMM1 tiles][W2 units][GEMM2 tiles]. CTAs claim items from an atomic head one item ahead. Each item
  waits only on self-resetting per-image counters (w1_done, conv_done[b], g1_done[b], w2_done), so there is no grid barrier.
  The aim was to pack the conv, the GEMM1 tails and the GEMM2 of different images onto the same SMs. Measured result:
  REFUTED in this form. Per-item CTA-time summed over the queue and divided by 148 SMs already exceeds D's whole-row time
  (47 / 111.5 / 71.9 us at 8,768 / 32,768 / 16,384). Each item runs claim, first TMA load, mainloop, epilogue and release
  serially on its own CTA, which costs 11.8-15.9 us per GEMM1 tile and about 14.6 us per GEMM2 tile.
expected_effect:
  S: {pct: 0, confidence: high}
  M: {pct: 75, confidence: high}
  L: {pct: 85, confidence: high}
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 156
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 205824
  threads_per_cta: 256
  ctas_per_sm: 1
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 196608
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs: {NTH: 256, NST: 4, STAGE: 49152, IPT1_C768: 2, N1_C768: 128, N1_C384: 208, KS2: 2, PG: "32 (B=8, C=384) / 64 (16,768) / 128 (32,768)", TMEM_cols: 512}
dispatch:
  - {rows: "8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768 (7x7) and 8,384 / 16,384 (14x14)", kernel: hk::h_kernel, meta: {C768: "<768,7>", C384: "<384,14>"}}
  - {rows: "all other 11", kernel: convnext_fused (r0 anchor, fallback only; merge-only candidate)}
tests: [H38, H10]
findings:
  - "run_tests 16/16 PASS (portal-order re-runs included). In the same container vs r7-merge, rented us: 8,768 65.3 vs 34.4 (+90 %); 16,768 81.5 vs 45.8 (+78 %); 32,768 123.3 vs 63.8 (+93 %); 8,384 74.2 vs 37.5 (+98 %); 16,384 90.8 vs 57.5 (+58 %). The other 11 rows run the r0 anchor, so the 0.414 prediction is meaningless; the merge should take NONE of the five rows [run_tests]"
  - "H38 verdict: success line missed on every row; the incubation line (within 15 % on 16,384 and 8,384) also missed (+58 % / +98 %). Refutation clause, first half fires: more than 10 % slower on every B>=8 wide-C row. Second half is mixed: W2 units fill the GEMM1 tails, and 18/96 (8,768), 60/192 (16,384) and 0/384 (32,768) GEMM2 items start before the last GEMM1 item ends. The dataflow family with whole-CTA serial items is closed for the wide-C rows; the value left is in D's engine terms [probe_b200, run_tests]"
  - "Decisive arithmetic from the stamps (v3): summed item CTA-time / 148 = 47.0 us (8,768), 111.5 (32,768), 71.9 (16,384) against D's whole rows 34.4 / 63.8 / 57.5. Perfect packing cannot win; the per-item cost structure is the binding term, not barriers [probe_b200]"
  - "Per-item costs (v3, us median, globaltimer from thread 0): GEMM1 tile at 8,768 (N=128, 12 k-blocks): dependency wait 2.05, mainloop 3.6, epilogue pass 1 (LN fold + erff GELU + sumsq + fp16 staging) 3.1-4.4, pass 2+3 (gf, h16/g16 coalesced stores) + release 2.8-3.6, about 12.5 total. At 16,384 (N=208, 6 k-blocks): mainloop 2.6, pass 1 5.9-8.5. GEMM2 tile at 8,768 (KS=4, 12 k-blocks, two accumulators, 48 KB stages): mainloop 5.6-6.1, epilogue 6.9-7.4. conv unit 3.3 (PG=32, 7x7) to 7.9 (PG=128 7x7 or PG=32 14x14). Weight units 4-17 us depending on version (see below) [probe_b200]"
  - "Queue mechanics are cheap, as the counter microbench predicted: claim-to-start (dependency wait with deps already satisfied) is 1.0-2.0 us median, the inter-item gap 1.5-3.3 us per CTA, total dependency spin 1.1-1.9k CTA-us per row (5-15 % of item time). STEP 0's standalone microbench was not run separately; these in-kernel numbers replace it [probe_b200]"
  - "GEMM2 epilogue: 16K scalar red.add per item cost about 4 of 7.4 us (store ablation 3.3 us). KS2=2 beats KS2=4 by 7-10 us per C=768 row (8,768 65.2 vs 74.5; 16,768 80.8 vs 90.7; 32,768 121.5 vs 128.3), because total atomics scale with split-K. Shipped with KS2=2 [probe_b200]"
  - "LN-statistics prestage: a runtime-bounded loop over NG partial groups (unroll 4) ran as ~6 serial L2 rounds. GEMM1 'mainloop' was 10 us at 8,768 (NG=24) and 6.9 at 16,384. A fully unrolled predicated load array (one round) cut it to 3.6-3.8 / 2.6 us [probe_b200]"
  - "Dead end: weight conversion with warp_sum shuffles inside an '#pragma unroll 8' load loop serialised the loads: W1 units went 5 -> 14.6 us and W2 units 6-10 -> 13-21 us. Fix: load JB=8 float4 per thread into register arrays first, shuffle afterwards. W2 units still take 11-17 us, which suggests the out = x + b2' prefill (37 scalar loads per thread, runtime division) is the slow part [probe_b200]"
  - "Writer-side fence.proxy.async (full) vs fence.proxy.async.shared::cta at item ends, with the consumer doing ld.acquire + fence.proxy.async before its TMA: only ~1 us difference, and both are correct on 16/16. The CUTLASS-style release (bar.sync then red.release.gpu from thread 0, no __threadfence) works for TMA consumers in other CTAs [probe_b200, run_tests]"
  - "Engine validated on the first build (STEP 1 folded into the kernel): tcgen05 kind::f16, swap-AB, A = 128x64 K-major SW128 box (SBO 1024, +32 B per k16), B = [channel][token] MN-major 64-token chunks (LBO 8192, SBO 1024, +2048 per k16), idesc = (1<<4)|(1<<16)|(N>>3)<<17|(128>>4)<<24, N = 64/128/208/80. task.instructions: Experiment E3 (tests H38): New design: image-counter dataflow persistent tcgen05 kernel (work queue, no grid barrier) for the B >= 8 wide-C rows. Rows 8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768 (7x7, C=768) and 8,384 / 16,384 (14x14, C=384); other rows run the r0 anchor fallback (merge-only candidate). Read the notebook and the lineage conclusions (D, B, F, C) first: the engine and the counter protocol are both documented there. STEP 0 (<= 5 min): queue/counter microbench, 148 cooperative CTAs with stub items (32 KB bulk copy each) in the proposed order and per-image gating, at B = 8 and 32, vs two flat-counter barriers; record the span and the median claim-to-start latency (expect <= 1 us). STEP 1 (engine, <= 15 min): a self-contained tcgen05 kind::f16 swap-AB tile (A = 128 weight rows K-major via a 128B-swizzled TMA box, B = activations [channel][token] MN-major with the validated descriptor: LBO 8192, SBO 1024, +2048 per k16; 4-stage ring; whole-warp TMA and MMA roles with elect.sync; accumulator in TMEM; tcgen05.ld with two loads in flight per thread), validated bit-close against torch (fp32 matmul of the fp16 operands, max err <= 2e-5) at 768x196x384 and 384x196x1536, warm L2, before any fusion. STEP 2 (kernel): one cooperative launch, 148 CTAs x 384-512 threads, 1 CTA/SM, dynamic smem set to the maximum over all shapes at module load. Workspace from torch.empty: queue head, w_done, conv_done[B], g1_done[B], departure counter, plus the fp16 W1'/W2 scratch, d16 and LN partials, hidden [k][token] fp16, gsq[B][4C]. Items in the static queue, claimed by atomicAdd on the head: (i) weight units: W1' = fp16(lnw-folded W1) with u = W1.lnw and c1 = W1.lnb + b1, W2 fp16, b2' = W2.gb + b2 and the out = x + b2' prefill (16-B loads/stores, spread over all CTAs); (ii) conv units: bulk-plane 7x7 / 14x14 depthwise conv of one plane group of ONE image plus per-token LN partials, so conv_done[b] counts units of image b; (iii) GEMM1 tiles (128 hidden rows x the tokens of one image, image-major): wait w_done == W units and conv_done[b] == units(b) with an ld.acquire poll, run the tile, epilogue = LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + c1, exact erf GELU (A&S erfc form accepted), per-(image,k) sumsq thread-local (lane = k) red.add into gsq[b][k], fp16 h stores coalesced through smem, then red.release.gpu on g1_done[b]; (iv) GEMM2 tiles (128 output channels x image tokens x split-K slice, image-major): wait g1_done[b] == tiles1(b), compute s_b = 1 + gw*gf/(mean gf + eps) from gsq[b] (one round, all loads issued first), scale the fp16 B stage in smem after it lands (fence.proxy.async before the MMA) or use D's two-accumulator form, red.global.add.v4 into out. The last departing CTA zeroes every counter so the workspace is correct for the next call. Keep every role warp-uniform; stamp phases from the working warps; check cuobjdump STACK 0. Compile with target_hardware [B200] only. STEP 3: stamps at 16,384 and 32,768 showing GEMM2 items of early images starting before the last GEMM1 items, and the per-CTA idle (spin) time. STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, r7-merge as the same-container control, PRECISION LOG (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds) for the five rows. Report per-row rented times vs the merge, the stamps, the microbench, registers/smem, and which rows (if any) the merge should take; negative results in full. Success: First build correct on all five rows and, in one container vs r7-merge, >= 5 us faster on at least one of 16,384 / 32,768 / 8,384 with stamps showing GEMM2 items running before the last GEMM1 items; 0 beyond-own-atol. Incubation line: within 15 % of the merge on 16,384 and 8,384 with the overlap visible in the stamps keeps the lineage alive for r9. Refuted if: With a validated engine, the packed kernel is slower than the merge by > 10 % on every B >= 8 wide-C row AND the stamps show the GEMM1 tails are not filled by GEMM2 or conv items (then the dataflow family is closed for the wide-C rows, and the remaining value is in the engine terms D already owns). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules, overrides the counter placement above): (a) torch.empty memory is uninitialised and is not guaranteed to be the same memory or unchanged between calls, so the queue head, w_done, conv_done[B], g1_done[B] and the departure counter must NOT live in the torch.empty workspace relying on the previous call's reset. Put them in a module-level __device__ buffer (zero-initialised at module load, sized for the largest B), reset by the last departing CTA after every other CTA has departed; or zero them with cudaMemsetAsync on the current stream immediately before the launch. (b) gsq[b][4C] and every other red.add target must be zeroed inside this call before its first add, ordered by a counter the adding items already wait on (e.g. zeroed in the weight units and covered by w_done). (c) W1'/W2/b2' scratch is rebuilt every call by the weight units (no converted weights kept across calls); TMA descriptors encoded every call. (d) Spin-waits rely on all CTAs being co-resident: cooperative launch with grid <= SM count, and every queue item may only wait on items with lower queue indices. (c) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes/plans.

task.instructions:
Experiment E2 (tests H33): GEMM2 as cta_group::2 pairs with a 6-stage half-tile ring in which g is produced by look-ahead warps, removing g from the GEMM1 epilogue (tc_kernel). STEP 0 (control and stamps, ~5 B200 min). Build the parent; run_tests once as the same-container control. Stamp GEMM2 per unit from the MMA warp and the drain warps: unit start, first stage landed, per-stage MMA issue (clock64 deltas, report clk per stage against the two-MMA ideal 2 x 2N clk per 64-k stage), mainloop end, drain end, red.add end; rows 8,768 / 32,768 / 16,384 / 2,768. Check STACK on the stamped build.
STEP 1 (pairs). Launch the cooperative kernel with cluster dims 2x1 (cudaLaunchKernelEx with both the cooperative and the cluster-dimension attributes; if the driver rejects the combination, fall back to a plain launch with grid <= residency checked per shape via cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters, and the flat self-resetting counter barrier for the two syncs, as F/H did). GEMM2 in the pair form from the lineage's validated recipe: M = 256 output channels across the pair (C=768: 3 pair M-tiles; C=384: one full pair tile plus one with 128 valid rows, A OOB zero-filled, epilogue masked, or keep the 1SM path for the 14x14 rows if the waste shows in the stamps), each CTA TMAs its own 128 A rows (W2, 16 KB per 64-k) and HALF of the B token tile (h 8 KB + g 8 KB) to the leader's full barrier via mapa, leader-only expect_tx of both CTAs' bytes, idesc M = 256>>4, tcgen05.commit .cta_group::2 .multicast::cluster mask 3, each CTA drains its own 128 TMEM lanes. Stage = 32 KB per CTA, ring depth 6. Retune KS per row so pair-units >= 74 x 1-2 (fewer, larger units than the 1SM version: 2 units per CTA at 32,768 today) and keep the coalesced red.add.v4 into the prefilled out. Validate vs torch on all six tc rows before timing. Stamp: clk per stage vs ideal and the GEMM2 phase per row.
STEP 2 (g out of GEMM1). GEMM1 epilogue writes h16 only and gw*gf per (image,k) into a [B][4C] fp32 array (the r8 smem-g variant did this: GEMM1 post -56 %). In GEMM2, 4 producer warps (not the drain warps, not the MMA warp) wait each stage's full barrier, build g16 = fp16(c[k] * h16) for the CTA's half tile (8 KB: 32 lanes x 4 warps x 64 B) into the stage's g buffer with c[k] = gw[k]*gf[img(token)][k] loaded once per unit into smem (one image group per N tile; at 7x7 N spans several images, so c is per (image, k) and the producer indexes by token column), issue fence.proxy.async.shared::cta, then arrive on a per-stage g_ready mbarrier; the MMA warp waits g_ready instead of full. The producers run up to STAGES-2 stages ahead (they only need landed h, which the 6-deep TMA ring provides). Measure clk per stage again: the gating of r8 (~0.8 us per stage) must be gone. If a stage still exceeds 1.3x the two-MMA ideal, build the fallback: one accumulator, the half h tile scaled in place by s_b (sc_kernel form, h rounded twice), 32 KB stages of A 16 + h 16 at depth 6, and compare both forms on the stamps and the rows.
STEP 3 (measure and ship). Interleave parent vs candidate x3 in one container on the 6 tc rows (and confirm the 7 sc rows are untouched). run_tests 16/16 incl. portal-order re-runs. PRECISION LOG (mandatory, the roundings may change): fp64 reference, harness generators, torch.manual_seed(200), 10 rounds per row, max |err| vs own atol and beyond-own-atol count for all six tc rows and the shipped form; if the fallback form ships and any row exceeds 90 % of its atol, scale the A tile from fp32 W2 instead. Record: stage clk vs ideal for 1SM / pair / pair+smem-g, GEMM2 phase per row, GEMM1 post-accumulator per tile, interleaved deltas, smem and register budgets (512 threads, <= 128 regs, STACK 0). Success: GEMM2 per 64-k stage <= 1.3x the two-MMA ideal on the stamps at 8,768 and 32,768; GEMM1 post-accumulator per tile >= 40 % below the parent; interleaved x3 rows: 16,384 <= 46, 8,384 <= 30, 32,768 <= 57, 16,768 <= 39, 8,768 <= 29, 2,768 <= 24 us rented; 16/16 pass; precision log <= 90 % of own atol with 0 beyond on every tc row. Refuted if: Pairs alone cut the GEMM2 phase by < 2 us at 8,768 and 32,768 AND neither smem-g form brings the stage under 1.5x the ideal, so the rows end within 1.5 us of the parent on 4 or more of the 6 tc rows (then GEMM2 at 7x7 is bound by the per-unit fixed chain, TMEM alloc + first landing + drain + red, and the next lever is fewer units per row, not stage bytes). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) gsq / gw*gf arrays and every red.add target are zeroed or written inside this launch before first use, ordered by a grid sync. (b) If the cooperative+cluster launch is rejected and you fall back to a plain launch, check co-residency per shape (grid <= cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters x 2) every call. Any grid-barrier counter, generation word or flag must live in a module-level __device__ buffer (zero-initialised at module load) and be self-reset by the last arriver, never in the torch.empty workspace (uninitialised, not guaranteed to be the same memory or unchanged between calls). Spin with plain ld.acquire loops, no __nanosleep. (z) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (TC_STAMPS/SC_STAMPS 0; the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. TMA descriptors encoded on every call. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes and plans set to one maximal value.

task.instructions:
Experiment E3 (tests H40): tcgen05 kind::f16 GEMM1 in the single-tile fused kernel g_p1s for 8,320,32,32 and 4,96,56,56. STEP 0 (engine gate, ~10 B200 min, standalone probe). From the notebook recipe (H r8: idesc = (1<<4)|(1<<16)|(N>>3)<<17|(128>>4)<<24; A = 128x64 K-major SW128 box, SBO 1024, +32 B per k16; B = [channel][token] MN-major 64-token chunks, LBO 8192, SBO 1024, +2048 per k16; whole-warp TMA and MMA roles with elect.sync; tcgen05.alloc 512 columns then relinquish; tcgen05.ld 32x32b.x32 with the wait in one asm) build a one-CTA kernel that writes the B tile into smem with PLAIN st.shared in the canonical swizzled MN-major layout (the conv warps will write d16 this way, not via TMA), TMAs A from an fp16 W1' buffer, runs K = 128 (C=96 padded with zero channels) and K = 320 (5 k-blocks), N = 128, and compares the TMEM result bit-for-bit against torch fp16 matmul with fp32 accumulation (<= 1e-3 relative). Do not proceed until this passes on both K values; record the swizzle address function used by the writers.
STEP 1 (g_p1s port). Conv warps write the fp16 d tile directly into the SW128 MN-major layout from STEP 0 (drop the token permutation; the LN stats path is unchanged). Zero the pad channels 96..127 in the d tile at C=96 once per tile buffer. A operand: W1' from the K0 fp16 scratch via a TMA ring (C=320: 10 hidden blocks x 5 k-blocks of 16 KB, 4-stage ring replacing the bulk ring; C=96: 3 hidden blocks x 2 k-blocks = 96 KB, resident after one TMA load per CTA at kernel start, or ring-fed if smem is short). One MMA warp (warp-uniform role; only the issue inside elect.sync) walks hidden blocks: at 4,96 N=128 tokens x 3 hidden blocks = 384 TMEM columns in one shot; at 8,320 (64-token tiles) 10 blocks x 64 columns = 640 > 512, so two 256-column accumulator halves (blocks 0-3 / 4-7 / 8-9) ping-ponged with per-half commit barriers, so the epilogue of one half overlaps the MMA of the next. Epilogue on every non-conv warp: tcgen05.ld (TMEM lane = hidden row, columns = tokens: each thread holds one hidden row x 32 tokens, so the fp16 h store is one contiguous 64 B per thread per load, no transpose), LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + c1 with per-token (mu, rs) from smem and per-row (u, c1) in registers, A&S erfc GELU, per-(image,k) sumsq thread-local then red.add per tile as now, h16 store. Keep the double-buffered d tile so the conv of tile i+1 overlaps the MMA+epilogue of tile i. Budget: <= 128 regs at the current thread count, STACK 0, smem <= 227 KB (print both per instantiation). target_hardware [B200] only.
STEP 2 (measure). Stamps from the working warps at 8,320 and 4,96: conv end, first MMA issue, per-half MMA done, epilogue end, tile end; then per-launch harness_time (K0 / +P1 / +K3 / +G2) with the 6-try CUPTI retry wrapper. Interleave parent vs candidate x3 in one container at 4,96 and 8,320; confirm 64,96 / 32,128 are byte-identical paths (g_pass1 untouched) and unchanged within noise. run_tests 16/16 incl. portal-order re-runs.
STEP 3 (precision and report). PRECISION LOG for 4,96 and 8,320 (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds, max |err| vs own atol, beyond count); the accumulation order changes with the engine, so the log is mandatory. Record: engine gate result, stage clk vs the kind::f16 ideal, pass 1 per row, interleaved deltas, resources, and whether the same port is feasible for g_pass1 at 64,96 / 32,128 (smem for W1' ring + d double buffer at R=2 tiles, TMEM columns at N=224). Success: Pass 1 <= 30 us at 8,320 and <= 19 us at 4,96 on the stamps; interleaved x3 rows 8,320 <= 55 and 4,96 <= 33 us rented (r8: 67.2 / 37.0); 16/16 pass; precision log 0 beyond own atol on both rows; 64,96 / 32,128 unchanged. Refuted if: The engine gate passes but pass 1 at 8,320 improves by < 6 us (the mma.sync term was 16.2 us, so the epilogue or the A ring must then be the new binding term: report the stamp), or the port cannot fit the register/smem budget without dropping the double-buffered d tile. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) the GRN sums and every red.add target are zeroed by K0 in the same call; W1' fp16 scratch written by K0 every call. (b) cuBLASLt: only the heuristic result may be cached per shape; descriptors, strides and pointers set every call, as r7/r8 do. (z) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (TC_STAMPS/SC_STAMPS 0; the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. TMA descriptors encoded on every call. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes and plans set to one maximal value.
